articles.title: Australia: Rising sea levels threaten more than 267,000 properties
articles.summary: BRISBANE — More than 267,000 Australian properties and two million hectares of land could be damaged or lost to rising sea levels and coastal flooding, in a trend that could cost the nation…

blocks.text: BRISBANE — More than 267,000 Australian properties and two million hectares of land could be damaged or lost to rising sea levels and coastal flooding, in a trend that could cost the nation $855 billion.

Western Australia faces the greatest economic losses by 2100 at $230.5 billion, while Queensland has the most properties at risk, with more than 93,000 on the line, followed by NSW with more than 71,000.
The Climate Council issued the warning on Thursday in a report estimating the financial cost of rising sea levels and storm surges, drawing on research from the University of Melbourne.

It comes one week after the United Nations warned the world would exceed 1.5 degrees of warming within years, increasing the risk of sea-level rises and more frequent extreme weather events such as heatwaves, cyclones, floods and fires.
The council’s report, Rising Seas, Rising Bills, estimated the risk of sea-level rises in Australia in an intermediate scenario where global emissions peaked in 2040 and declined rapidly.

It found Australia could suffer $274.3 billion in property losses by 2100 because of inundation of low-lying areas, coastal flooding and land erosion, with effects felt in every state and the Northern Territory.

Damage to land could cost $580.7 billion, with more than 619,000 hectares of farmland at risk, along with more than 379,000 hectares of parks and recreation areas, and more than 23,000 hectares of land hosting critical infrastructure.
Scientists predicted sea levels would rise by at least another 14 centimeters by 2050, Climate Council spokesman Andrew Watkins said, but the actual figure could be higher and the risks greater.

“These are big, big numbers that we need to consider and the economic part of the study is conservative in that it doesn’t account for everything that could happen but for the basic land, property and infrastructure costs,” he told AAP.
“What we want is for people to realise what is at stake here.”
Western Australia, with the biggest coastline, faced the biggest risk of economic loss with more than 586,000 hectares of land exposed to rising seas and storm surges.

But Queensland had the highest number of properties at risk, the report said, with the Gold Coast named the most exposed urban area in Australia, facing the loss of more than 32,000 properties and $84 billion.
Private insurance rarely covered “actions of the sea”, the report noted, and could leave residents with high damage bills.

The federal government should stop approving fossil fuel projects and strengthen emission cuts to avert further risks, Mr Watkins said, but should also work with state and local governments to prevent construction in at-risk areas and preserve coastal regions.
“It is a creeping problem that’s not as obvious as fire and floods and you don’t want to suddenly, too late, realise what the impacts might be,” he said.
“We need to plan now and the sooner we get on to it, the better.”
Rising sea levels were already affecting agriculture in Australia, cane farmer Robert Quirk said.
His land in NSW’s Tweed Valley sits half a meter above sea level, and rising tides mean he has to run pumps throughout the year to drain the fields.
“We have a drainage problem and for every centimetre the ocean rises, I pump another 10 Olympic swimming pools off the farm every rain event,” he said.
“I’ve got little grandchildren who’ll be alive in 2100 and what will they do?” /dl

articles.summary: The prosecution accuses Vice President Sara Duterte of betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution over her unexplained wealth

The prosecution accuses Vice President Sara Duterte of betrayal of public trust and culpable violation of the Constitution over her unexplained wealth

items: The prosecution in Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial plans to call witnesses including a former anti-graft court justice and representatives from the Office of the Ombudsman and SEC to testify about her alleged unexplained wealth.

Key witnesses will discuss public accountability, details of Duterte's financial declarations, and authenticate company records linked to her, with the prosecution potentially presenting up to 25 witnesses and 1,800 financial documents.

Duterte faces accusations of violating the Constitution and betraying public trust due to discrepancies between her bank transactions and net worth declarations, with the Anti-Money Laundering Council reporting suspicious transactions totaling P6.77 billion.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The prosecution team in the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte seeks to present a former anti-graft court justice, as well as representatives from the Office of the Ombudsman and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), as its first witnesses in its unexplained wealth case against her.
Prosecutor Terry Ridon told the media on Thursday, September 10, that they have requested from the impeachment court the issuance of subpoenas to the following individuals:

items: Retired Sandiganbayan presiding justice Amparo Cabotaje-Tang
Office of the Ombudsman Records Division Officer-in-Charge Karen Batu
SEC Company Registration and Monitoring Department Director Gerardo del Rosario

blocks.caption: Ex-Sandiganbayan justice among first witnesses in Sara Duterte unexplained wealth case

blocks.text: Ridon said Cabotaje-Tang will be asked to discuss the principles governing public accountability and integrity, as well as mechanisms for addressing undisclosed wealth.

Batu will testify on specific details about Duterte’s Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN), while Del Rosario will authenticate the company records associated with the Vice President, Ridon added.
The list of intended prosecution witnesses is still subject to the approval of the impeachment court. The trial resumes on Monday, September 14.
Prosecutor Joel Chua previously said that their team may present up to 25 witnesses for the second impeachment article, alongside 1,800 financial documents.

Duterte is accused of culpable violation of the Constitution and betrayal of public trust when she supposedly amassed unexplained wealth, highlighted by supposed inconsistencies between the Vice President’s large bank transactions and her net worth declarations.

The Anti-Money Laundering Council had said that according to the banks, the accounts named under the Vice President and her husband, Mans Carpio, were the subject of covered transaction reports and suspicious transaction reports amounting to P6.77 billion from 2006 to 2025.
Duterte’s legal team questioned the presentation of the AMLC numbers, saying an aggregate of inflows and outflows over two decades would naturally yield a bloated number.
Despite the billions of pesos in bank transactions over the years, Duterte’s net worth averaged P42 million in 15 years, peaking at P88 million in 2024.

What’s more notable is that she made zero cash and cash declaration deposits from 2019 to 2024, and modest cash on hand and cash in bank declarations during years she was in elective office between 2007 and 2018. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Civic Circles: How can we keep our children and schools safe?
articles.summary: The panel discussion starting at 12:30 pm on September 10 brings together stakeholders to identify safety gaps and develop community-led solutions to protect children

blocks.text: LIVE

blocks.caption: Civic Circles: How can we keep our children and schools safe?

blocks.text: The panel discussion starting at 12:30 pm on September 10 brings together stakeholders to identify safety gaps and develop community-led solutions to protect children
MANILA, Philippines – Concerned about your child’s safety and how you can ensure a more secure environment for them?

Watch the live panel discussion as Rappler’s civic engagement arm MovePH launches “Civic Circles: How can we keep our children and schools safe?” This will be streamed on Rappler’s YouTube channel live from the Rappler Civic Hub in Pasig City on Thursday, September 10.

Organized in partnership with CyberGuardiansPH and Mental Health Youth Hub, this pilot initiative tackles rising school violence and digital risks by turning community discussions into concrete, multisectoral solutions.
Rappler head of community Pia Ranada moderates the conversation with key decision-makers and child protection advocates:

items: Quezon City Mayor Joy Belmonte shares local government strategies on community governance, child protection policies, and campus safety.
Police Capt. Wallen Arancillo, spokesperson for the PNP Anti-Cybercrime Group, addresses online grooming, cyberbullying, and digital protection in off-campus hotspots.
Dr. Princess Gairanod, child protection specialist from the Philippine Pediatric Society, discusses student mental health, psychosocial care, and health safeguarding protocols.

Razzel Anne Requesto, Director IV at the Department of Education (DepEd) Office of the Assistant Secretary for Governance and Support Services, discusses institutional safety protocols and learner protection guidelines.

blocks.text: After the panel discussion and Q and A, participants joining on-site can take part in a hands-on workshop to collectively develop concrete and actionable responses to threats facing children and schools across four Civic Circles:

items: Campus security and physical safety
Psychosocial care and mental health
Policy, governance, and accountability
Digital safety and off-campus hotspots

blocks.text: The solutions generated during the session may be featured on Rappler to encourage a broader discussion and possible adaptation by local governments, schools, families, and communities.
Bookmark this page to watch Rappler’s live broadcast.
To join the conversation, download the Rappler App on iOS or Android, tap the Chat tab, and enter the Education chat room while watching the stream. – Rappler.com

articles.title: North Korea has built new uranium facility to expand nuclear arsenal, UN agency says
articles.summary:
The International Atomic Energy Agency voices ‘serious concerns’ over expansion of Yongbyon facility to enrich uranium

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has voiced “serious…

blocks.text: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has voiced “serious concern” over evidence that North Korea has built a facility capable of enriching weapons-grade uranium to bolster its nuclear arsenal.

The new building, located at the the country’s main Yongbyon nuclear facility, can house up to 28 centrifuge cascades – machinery commonly used to enrich uranium – according to a report by the nuclear watchdog released this week.

The regime has also expanded operations at an enrichment site in Kangson, near the capital Pyongyang, according to the report, which was based on analysis of satellite imagery and open-source material, including photographs published by the country’s state media.

The IAEA, whose inspectors were expelled from North Korea in 2009, identified the Yongbyon building as the site’s second uranium ‌enrichment facility after comparing satellite images taken during its construction with media photographs of a visit in early June by the country’s leader, Kim Jong-un.

blocks.caption: A satellite image from 4 September shows the nuclear material production factory in Yongbyon. Photograph: 2026 Planet Labs PBC/Reuters

blocks.text: During his visit, Kim claimed the North’s capacity to produce weapons-grade nuclear material had more than doubled over the past five years, according to state media, promising “vast future plans to exponentially strengthen the country’s nuclear forces”.

Citing a 2025 analysis by the James Martin Center for Nonproliferation Studies in the US, South Korea’s Chosun Daily said the potential 28 cascades comprising 4,592 centrifuges at the Yongbyon facility could yield about 85 kg of weapons-grade highly enriched uranium a year – enough to build three or four additional warheads.

In a statement released this week, the IAEA’s director general, Rafael Grossi, said: “The ongoing operation of enrichment facilities at Kangson and Yongbyon and the reported further expansion of [North Korea’s] production of weapons-grade nuclear material is a cause for serious concern.”
“The continuation and further development” of North Korea’s nuclear programme are “clear violations of relevant UN security council resolutions and are deeply regrettable”, he added.

South Korea’s defence minister, Ahn Gyu-back, said in August that the North possessed between 80 and 120 nuclear warheads – a much higher number than the 57 cited by Donald Trump the same month. The South Korean figure was based on estimates by private research organisations, Ahn told lawmakers, adding that the country’s military could not confirm the numbers.
North Korea has made rapid progress in its ballistic missile and nuclear programmes in recent years, as it demands international recognition as a legitimate nuclear state.

North Korea has conducted multiple long-range missile tests since 2017, the year it last tested a nuclear weapon. In a report submitted to the UN security council in 2020, international experts said the North had “probably developed nuclear devices to fit into the warheads of its ballistic missiles”.

articles.title: LTO-7 issues show cause order against SUV driver in fatal Barili crash
articles.summary: CEBU CITY, Philippines — The Land Transportation Office in Central Visayas (LTO-7) has issued a show cause order against the driver of a Barili municipal government-owned SUV, who was involved in a…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — The Land Transportation Office in Central Visayas (LTO-7) has issued a show cause order against the driver of a Barili municipal government-owned SUV, who was involved in a road crash that killed a 10-year-old boy and injured his 8-year-old companion.
The crash happened along the provincial road in Barangay Candugay, Barili, Cebu, at around 12:30 p.m. on Tuesday, September 8.

The LTO-7 order directs the driver and the registered owner, the Municipality of Barili, to appear before the agency’s Operations Division and explain why the driver should not be held administratively liable for reckless driving and why his driver’s license should not be suspended or revoked.
Pending the administrative investigation, LTO-7 also ordered the driver to immediately surrender his driver’s license and placed him under a 90-day preventive suspension.
The SUV involved in the crash has likewise been placed under alarm pending the outcome of the investigation.
LTO cites alleged overtaking before fatal collision
According to the show cause order, LTO-7 initiated the administrative investigation based on the police report from Barili Municipal Police Station.
The police report showed that the SUV was being driven along the provincial road when its driver allegedly attempted to overtake a motorcycle.
In the process, the SUV allegedly encroached into the opposite lane and collided with an approaching bicycle carrying the two minors.
Both boys sustained serious injuries from the collision.
The 10-year-old boy, who was riding the bicycle, was rushed to the hospital but was declared dead on arrival. His 8-year-old passenger was admitted to the hospital for treatment of his injuries.
Earlier information from authorities showed that the SUV was traveling from Barangay Candugay toward Barili proper when the crash occurred.
The vehicle is registered under the Municipality of Barili and was being driven by the town’s registered driver, a 37-year-old resident of Barangay Boloc-Boloc.
Driver ordered to explain

Under the show cause order, the Municipality of Barili, as the registered owner, and the designated driver were directed to appear before the LTO-7 Operations Division along N. Bacalso Avenue in Cebu City within five days upon receipt of the order.
They were also directed to submit beforehand a sworn comment or explanation, together with pertinent original documents, to rebut the allegations surrounding the crash.
LTO-7 ordered them to show cause why the driver should not be held administratively liable for reckless driving under Section 48 of Republic Act No. 4136, or the Land Transportation and Traffic Code.

The driver must also explain why his license should not be suspended or revoked for being an “Improper Person to Operate a Motor Vehicle” under Section 27(a) of RA 4136, as amended by Batas Pambansa Blg. 398.
The agency said its investigation could also establish liability for other violations in connection with the incident.

LTO-7 warned that failure to appear or submit the required comment or explanation would be considered a waiver of the respondents’ right to do so, after which the agency may proceed with and complete the investigation in their absence.
They may also be assisted by legal counsel during the investigation.
Criminal case expected
Separate from LTO-7’s administrative investigation, the 37-year-old driver remained detained at Barili Municipal Police Station following the fatal crash.
The parents of the 10-year-old victim have expressed their intention to pursue a case over their son’s death.
According to police, a case for reckless imprudence resulting in homicide is expected to be filed on Thursday, September 10.

The LTO administrative proceedings are focused on the driver’s possible liability under transportation laws and the status of his driving privilege, while authorities are separately pursuing the case arising from the boy’s death.

articles.title: James Reid goes full throttle with new album in the middle of TV, film projects
articles.summary: Singer-actor James Reid is enjoying a resurgence in his career as an entertainer in the Philippines, with a new album releasing in the middle of his hit teleserye “Someone, Someday,” with…

blocks.text: Singer-actor James Reid is enjoying a resurgence in his career as an entertainer in the Philippines, with a new album releasing in the middle of his hit teleserye “Someone, Someday,” with Kathryn Bernardo.
After his collaboration with crooner Maki “Luck” hit it big on Spotify with more than 1 million streams, Reid is delivering a full album dubbed “Honey, I’m Home” under Careless Music.

“I didn’t expect that I’d be releasing an album in the middle of a teleserye, and shooting a film at the same time,” he responded to Inquirer Entertainment when he shared the tracks on his new album at the record label’s studio in Makati City on Sept. 9.

“Honestly, it’s been so busy and hectic and draining. But I said this is the year I really wanted to make an impact, so I can’t really complain,” Reid continued, adding that Sony Music will be releasing his album Thursday, Sept. 10.

The project is a result of the songwriting camp that he and other musicians took part in for a couple of weeks in February last year. And although they were not working on a certain timeline to release an album, he said he felt that now is the time that it is ready to come out.

“It starts with a very simple concept, ‘Honey I’m Home.’ It’s really coming home. And home is not a place, it’s just being with someone you love, a place where you feel safe, a place where you feel loved, a place where you can be yourself,” Reid said.
The opening track of the same title, he said, lays the foundation of what the whole album hopes to achieve, with each track representing a certain room or part of one’s home.
“As I was finishing the project, towards the end, it became something different. The idea of home became more present, and learning just to be comfortable in my own skin,” Reid said.

“First I thought home was a person. And then I found that home is myself by the end of the album. And I thought, what if nothing was really missing in the first place? What if I just wasn’t home? What if I wasn’t just home with myself? So that’s what the album is in a nutshell,” he continued.
The album carries several collaborations as well. “Sunny Side” features Luke April, and Reid said it was one of his favorite tracks in the album. It was released two weeks ago to serve as a teaser.
He shared the microphone, and writing credits, with Arthur Nery for “All Night,” and Reid said there was nobody else that he had in mind to collaborate with for the the song but Nery.

“Indiana” is an emotional piece he wrote and performed with his girlfriend Issa Pressman, an anthem to a child they are yet to have but often talk about having. “We love this imaginary person that doesn’t exist yet, so much, and they’re not even here. So I want to write a song about that,” Reid explained.

“I want to make a song that kind of talks about a love that transcends generations. We love you even though you’re not here. Indiana is the name of the girl. And one day when we’re gone, the love will still be there,” he continued.

As for the carrier single, “Attention,” Reid said he wrote the song to show how attention is also a form of love and devotion. “Where attention goes, love grows. And I thought that sometimes the greatest thing that you can give someone is just your full presence and attention,” he said.

“Honey, I’m Home” has a balance of English and Filipino songs with an RnB flavor to it, and a little smattering of folk and country. “I’m not really looking to be understood in this album. I just want to make something for them and I hope they enjoy it, and it applies to them and their lives somehow, or they just love listening to it,” Reid said. /ra

articles.title: Asian Games: Robert Bolick urged to keep head up after Gilas setbacks
articles.summary: SCHEDULE: Gilas Pilipinas men at Asian Games 2026 5×5 basketball MANILA, Philippines–NLEX coach Jimmy Alapag made sure Robert Bolick would get his message across after Gilas Pilipinas’ much-maligned…

blocks.text: FILE– Robert Bolick during his stint with Gilas Pilipinas. –POC MEDIA
SCHEDULE: Gilas Pilipinas men at Asian Games 2026 5×5 basketball

MANILA, Philippines–NLEX coach Jimmy Alapag made sure Robert Bolick would get his message across after Gilas Pilipinas’ much-maligned showing in a two-game exhibition with South Korea raised doubts about its chances of retaining the gold in the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.

“I reached out to him after the second tune-up against Korea, and told him to keep his head up, to keep the guys together,” Alapag said after the Road Warriors’ 109-107 loss to the Blackwater Bossing in the PBA On Tour exhibition game in San Jose del Monte, Bulacan.
Gilas faced massive criticism from fans after it was blown out by an average of 26.5 points and never made things competitive during the series held in Suwon.
One of the players who came under fire was Bolick, who scored a total of four points on a combined 2-of-15 shooting on top of a two-game average of 3.5 rebounds and 3.5 assists.

Coach Tim Cone is banking on Bolick to lead the squad while also manning the backcourt, a role he did quite well during his previous national team stint last December at the Thailand Southeast Asian Games.

Alapag, the Gilas captain during the historic 2013 Fiba Asia Championship run and 2014 Fiba World Cup, believes Cone’s squad can use the tune-up matches to play the way it hopes to be for the Asian Games.
“It’s tough when you lose a tune-up game. But that’s what they’re for, diba? You just find ways to improve,” Alapag said.
“And I think for that team in particular, [you just have to] build off some chemistry and camaraderie before the tournament starts in Nagoya,” he added.
Gilas starts off its campaign on Friday against Bahrain, and Alapag acknowledges that Bolick and company will be in for a daunting task.
That doesn’t mean, however, that Gilas is going to play as it did against South Korea once the real games start.

“I’m still confident that [Robert] and the guys will go out there and represent the flag proudly for there country,” Alapag said. “But they got a tough road ahead. but I just want to let him know that all of us are rooting for them and supporting them.”

articles.title: Anthropic researcher quits over fears AI could kill off humanity
articles.summary: A British researcher has resigned from U.S. artificial intelligence developer Anthropic over fears that the race to develop “self-improving superintelligence” could lead to…

blocks.text: A British researcher has resigned from U.S. artificial intelligence developer Anthropic over fears that the race to develop “self-improving superintelligence” could lead to humanity’s extinction.

Jacob Coxon, who previously worked on pretraining research at OpenAI and Anthropic, posted on X on Tuesday that “neither company is acting responsibly,” and that the people building AI “earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.”

Evan Hubinger, alignment science lead at Anthropic, confirmed Coxon’s sentiments in his own X post, saying, “We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans! I personally think it is >10% within the next decade.”

Concerns over rogue AI have intensified following the Hugging Face incident in July, in which hundreds of OpenAI agents independently coordinated to break out of a secure testing environment and hack systems at the U.S. tech platform.

“Do not underestimate the power of this technology. These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources,” Coxon warned.

While there is potential for coordination among U.S. firms to slow the pace of AI development, preventing a global race “may require costly actions such as a temporary ban on improving model capabilities,” Coxon added.
Hubinger said that while Anthropic is trying its best to solve alignment for superintelligence, it does not currently have a plan, nor is it on track to. /dl

articles.title: King Harald V’s funeral: Norway bids farewell as crowds, royals converge
articles.summary: OSLO, Norway — Norway bade its final farewell to Harald V on Wednesday as crowds lined the streets and foreign royals and leaders converged on Oslo for the funeral of the long-serving king, who was…

blocks.text: OSLO, Norway — Norway bade its final farewell to Harald V on Wednesday as crowds lined the streets and foreign royals and leaders converged on Oslo for the funeral of the long-serving king, who was remembered as a popular monarch with a down-to-earth touch.

A 21-gun salute rang out over the capital at the start of a funeral procession from the royal palace to Oslo Cathedral. Harald’s son, new King Haakon VIII, and other senior royals walked behind the coffin, draped with the red Norwegian royal standard. Harald’s widow, Queen Sonja, and Haakon’s wife, Queen Mette-Marit, followed in a car.
Norwegian officials and foreign dignitaries joined the solemn procession. They included the monarchs of Sweden, Denmark, Spain, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Monaco and Jordan.

Also present were the heir to the British throne, Prince William, and Japan’s Crown Prince Akishino, as well as political leaders from more than 20 countries, including Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Harald V was a king who met people ‘in his rubber boots’
As the funeral service began, Norway came to a halt for a minute of silence.

Harald, who died on Aug. 28 aged 89, was Europe’s oldest monarch and had reigned for 35 years. He modernized the royal house but refused to follow in the footsteps of other aging monarchs who recently abdicated. His son immediately became king and last week took an oath of allegiance to Norway’s constitution in parliament.
The parliament’s speaker, Masud Gharahkhani, said at the service that “King Harald was close to the people” and recalled that “he wasn’t afraid to meet people in his rubber boots.”
He remembered Harald saying in his 2008 New Year’s address: “I wish we would stop using the term ‘the weakest in society.’ In reality, some of these people are among the strongest of us all.”
“He lived up to his motto: He gave his all for Norway,” Gharahkhani said.
Large crowds lined the streets ahead of the funeral

Large crowds flocked to Oslo for the funeral, and thousands stood behind barriers on streets lined with national flags. The downtown area was closed to vehicles and electric scooters, and police had instructed people not to bring bicycles, umbrellas or sharp objects.

People tuned in across the country of about 5.6 million. Scores of churches, libraries, cultural centers and city halls made big screens available for the public to watch the funeral, public broadcaster NRK reported. The government said it wasn’t an official holiday, but schools and workplaces could individually opt to let students and employees watch.

Ahead of the funeral, Norwegians waited patiently to file past Harald’s coffin in the chapel of the royal palace. The queue was seven hours long at one point over the weekend. Over 46,000 people visited the chapel during the week it lay in state.

“The love between the people and King Harald has not ended — quite the contrary,” said Bishop Olav Fykse Tveit, who led the funeral service, pointing to the tributes left outside the palace after his death. “The sea of flowers, along with the words and drawings that accompany them, speaks loudly and clearly of a heart so full that it overflows.”

After the funeral, Harald’s coffin was taken in a smaller procession to Akershus Fortress, where his predecessors are buried in the crypt of the palace chapel. Haakon followed with the two other Scandinavian monarchs, King Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden and King Frederik X of Denmark.

Among those who attended the funeral was Mette-Marit’s eldest son and Haakon’s stepson, Marius Borg Høiby, who has no royal title or duties. Høiby is appealing against a rape conviction after a trial earlier this year that cast a shadow over the royal family.

Norway’s monarchy traces its origins to King Harald Fairhair in the ninth century. When Norway regained its independence from Sweden in 1905, three-quarters of voters in a national plebiscite approved restoring the monarchy.

The Norwegian royal house has kinfolk in other European royal families. Harald and Haakon are related to both Britain’s King Charles III and Spain’s King Felipe VI: They’re all descendants of the U.K.’s Queen Victoria, who reigned from 1837 until her death in 1901.

Today, the throne’s role is largely symbolic and power lies with the elected government and parliament, but the Norwegian royal family retains a role in promoting the wealthy Scandinavian nation around the world. /dl

articles.title: UK disabled people could swap Pip cash for ‘in kind’ support in benefit overhaul
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Claimants could trade part of payment for specialist equipment, services or training under proposal

Some disabled people could receive “in kind” support rather than just cash…

blocks.text: Some disabled people could receive “in kind” support rather than just cash payments under a radical overhaul of the personal independence payment (Pip) proposed by official government advisers, the Guardian can reveal.

The proposal, from an expert committee largely made up of disabled people, is one of a number of striking “emerging recommendations” likely to form the basis of the government’s Timms review of Pip, expected to be published in the next two months.

Rather than automatically receive weekly cash payments, currently between £30.30 and £194.60 depending on need, some claimants could instead swap part of the cash award for specialist equipment and aids, services, or skills and training.

Pip would remain non-means-tested, but while cash would remain “the foundation” of the award, the idea that claimants would be offered the choice of practical rather than just financial support marks a potentially radical departure in welfare policy.

The committee does not address the costs of Pip – currently about £23bn a year – and does not discuss potential cuts in spending, although it acknowledges its reforms must stay within current Pip spending projections of £41bn a year by 2029.

Although political and media debate has focused on the affordability of increases in Pip spending, the committee has focused primarily on improving people’s experience of Pip and better supporting ill and disabled people to participate in every day life.
Other recommendations include:

Introducing a fast-track process to allow new claimants with a terminal illness to claim Pip more speedily – and reducing the number of benefit reassessments for people with lifelong or degenerative conditions.
Reviewing strict and “unnecessarily stressful” rules that suspend an individual’s Pip award automatically after they have spent more than 28 consecutive days in hospital.
Improving the way Pip assesses fluctuating issues such as mental illness to adequately capture the impact of conditions that vary over time.

While Pip is vital to help disabled people meet the extra costs of disability, it should also support individuals to live independently and help give them choice, dignity and control over their lives, the committee says.

Pip should be tailored more closely to individuals’ needs and requirements, offering a wider range of support to help them achieve “participation and opportunity across every day life” including work, care and volunteering, it adds.

The 12-strong committee of expert advisers, the majority of whom have lived experience of disability or long-term health conditions, are at the heart of a review commissioned to redesign the Pip benefit after the disastrous collapse of Labour’s planned cuts to disability benefits last year.

A backbench rebellion forced the government into a U-turn on £5bn of cuts in the summer of 2025, amid public opposition to plans that would have slashed household incomes and pushed hundreds of thousands of people with disabilities into poverty.

The subsequent review of Pip, co-chaired by the welfare minister, Sir Stephen Timms, published an interim report in July this year which concluded that Pip was unfit for purpose and too often left vulnerable claimants feeling dehumanised rather than supported.

Pip, which is claimed by nearly 4 million people in England and Wales, is designed to help claimants with the extra costs of disability, such as energy, transport and food. It is not linked to employment status, and about a sixth of claimants are in work.

The committee insists the emerging recommendations are not final but will be tested for fairness and workability in a series of workshops involving thousands of people with disabilities across the UK to be held over the next few weeks.

There may be resistance among campaigners to introducing non-cash elements within Pip awards. However, recent polling of Pip recipients by the Good Growth Foundation thinktank found half supported the principle of swapping part of their cash payment for services such as skills and training, home adaptations or therapy.

The committee’s recommendations are likely to be closely scrutinised by a separate review of the youth jobs crisis by former Labour MP Alan Milburn, who has made it clear that some of the cash spent on benefits for young people should be redirected towards providing them with training and skills.

A Department for Work and Pensions spokesperson said: “These are not the final recommendations. The review will report to the secretary of state this autumn and he will carefully consider the final proposals within it.
“The Timms review interim report, co-produced with disabled people, made clear that Pip is no longer fit for purpose.
“Our goal is to deliver a system that supports disabled people and those with long-term conditions to live independent lives, while remaining fair, sustainable and fit for the future.”

articles.title: ‘Fundamentally unfair’: Burnham must overhaul migration reforms, says TUC general secretary
articles.summary:
Paul Nowak says changes to immigration rules risk overstretching social care and fuelling far-right sentiment

Andy Burnham must overhaul Shabana Mahmood’s migration reforms or risk…

blocks.text: Andy Burnham must overhaul Shabana Mahmood’s migration reforms or risk overstretching social care and fuelling far-right sentiment, the TUC general secretary, Paul Nowak, has warned.

Speaking ahead of the TUC’s annual congress in Brighton next week, Nowak welcomed the “sense of optimism” around Burnham’s fledgling government, but he urged the PM to act in a series of areas, including migration and the cost of living.

Burnham reappointed Mahmood as home secretary when he became prime minister in July. Her department is consulting on proposals that would force more than 300,000 low-paid workers to wait 15 years for the legal right to remain in the UK.
These include many carers who came to the UK to fill vacancies after the Covid pandemic, and were told they could apply for indefinite leave to remain after five years.
“I think it is fundamentally unfair to change the rules when people came to this country with one set of expectations,” Nowak said. “I hope we can think again on that.”

He added: “There are 111,000 staff vacancies in social care at the moment. I want us to train up as many Brits as possible to do those jobs. But I suspect in a growing economy with an ageing population, we are still going to need people to come and live and work in the UK and work in sectors like social care.”
As well as criticising the backward-looking changes, Nowak also condemned the idea of applying a 10- or 15-year wait to many new arrivals, as the Home Office has proposed.

“Both my granddads came to this country after the second world war – one came from Hong Kong, one came from Poland. Both raised their families here. The idea that you could be here for the next 10, 15 years and you’d still have no legal right to remain in the country … how the hell do you plan? Can you buy a house? What does that mean for your employment? Do you have kids? Do you send them to school? I mean, it cuts across any effort to integrate at all.”

Labour politicians supportive of the changes see them partly as a way of assuaging public concerns about migration, and neutralising the appeal of populist parties, including Nigel Farage’s Reform UK.
But Nowak suggested that by significantly lengthening the time before people can consider themselves settled in the UK, the approach could ultimately fuel far-right sentiment.

“I tell you where you end up: you end up with Reform claiming that a woman who was born in Somalia and has lived here for most of her life and worked hard and contributed to our society, somehow isn’t fit to hold elected office in this country.”

Reform UK’s home affairs spokesperson, Zia Yusuf, was recently accused of “straightforward racism” by Labour after he suggested the party’s frontrunner to replace Keir Starmer in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection, former child refugee Sagal Abdi-Wali, was not British.

blocks.caption: Sagal Abdi-Wali (centre) at an anti-Brexit march. Photograph: Martin Plaut

blocks.text: Nowak acknowledged that many TUC members will have backed Reform in recent local elections, but suggested the party’s appeal may be waning.

“Our members are a broad cross section of the British public. Of course, large numbers of them voted Reform, like other people did. But certainly the evidence that we’re getting fed back from unions is that just like the British public, the more they see of Nigel Farage, the less keen they are.”
after newsletter promotion

Nowak claimed there was a “direct line” from the rhetoric of Farage and his allies, to what he called the “proto-fascism” of the balaclava-clad vigilantes who blocked infrastructure in Dover and tried to stop migrants arriving in Portsmouth last weekend.
He suggested Labour should focus on cost-of-living issues to combat Reform’s populist appeal – including offering voters more help with rising energy bills.

“The most important thing that Andy Burnham can do is to deliver the change that people voted for back in July 2024. If people feel that the government is taking the stuff that matters to them seriously and is delivering on it, I think it cuts the legs from underneath that rightwing populism.”

Ahead of the budget on 28 October, Nowak called for a “social tariff” to cut energy bills for lower paid users, funded by a windfall tax on the banks. “As well as delivering a boost to hundreds of thousands of households up and down the country, it will help bear down on the cost of inflation,” he said.
“The public bailed the banks out in 2008. For those families who are worried about turning on the heating this year, asking the banks to pay their fair share isn’t unreasonable.”

A Home Office spokesperson said: “last November, we set out reforms to double the standard qualifying period for settlement to 10 years for most migrants, with shorter routes for those who contribute most to the UK.
“A consultation on elements of those reforms has now closed, and we will set out our response in due course.”

articles.title: ‘Institutional neglect’: 25 years on from 9/11, experts sound alarm over US counter-terror efforts
articles.summary:
Budget cuts, loss of knowledgeable officials and diverted resources raise risk of another attack, experts warn

The US faces growing challenges in countering international terrorism as…

blocks.text: The US faces growing challenges in countering international terrorism as resources are diverted to other threats, experienced security officials leave and “complacency” spreads, experts have warned.

It is 25 years this week since the 9/11 attacks launched by Osama bin Laden’s al-Qaida on New York and Washington, which killed about 3,000 people and led to decades of conflict, radicalisation and instability across the Middle East and beyond.
Though there have been no successful attacks on anything like a similar scale in the US since, and only a small number inspired by extremist Islamist ideologies, many are warning of growing risks.

Some blame Donald Trump for politicising counter-terrorism efforts, making ill-considered and inappropriate appointments to senior intelligence posts and diverting attention from more urgent threats with a campaign against drug cartels.

blocks.caption: Members of the Mexican national guard and army patrol the border wall between Mexico and the US. Trump has shifted focus and resources by designating criminal groups such as the Mexican drug cartels as foreign terrorist organisations. Photograph: José Luis González/Reuters

blocks.text: Bruce Hoffman, a terrorism expert at Georgetown University, said: “I remember [9/11] and this pure chaos and pandemonium in the streets and I remember thinking that we would never lower our guard again and complacency against a threat that is episodic but when it is revealed highly consequential.”

This year, Hoffmann told the US House permanent select committee on intelligence that “the counter-terrorism architecture built after 9/11 is eroding … through budget cuts, personnel losses, and the diminution of terrorism as a national security priority”.
This was “recreating the conditions of under-resourcing and institutional neglect that preceded the 2001 attacks. Moreover, the terrorist threat to Americans has both changed and grown.”

Analysts are split over whether the lack of obvious recent efforts by al-Qaida to strike in the US suggests a lack of ambition or disguises a careful, strategic plan to wait for the right opportunity.

Last month, a UN report based on intelligence supplied by member states’ monitoring said the “al-Qaida senior leadership remained marginalized” while “its capability and intent to conduct external operations remained unclear”.
Colin Clarke, the executive director of the Soufan Center, said the US intelligence community was experiencing a “basket of factors” including “funding, personnel [and] complacency”.
“There is a certain amount of fatigue. We did the global war on terror for 20 years and people were keen to pivot to something else,” he said.

Most analysts support a 2018 shift away from terrorism to focus on “long-term, strategic competition by … revisionist powers” such as Russia and China. But choices made by the Trump administration have exacerbated existing problems.
“There is a real lack of morale because of the way the president has treated the intelligence community … the quiet professionals are really demoralised,” Clarke said.

blocks.caption: Intelligence veterans criticised the appointments of Tulsi Gabbard and Kash Patel to high-profile national intelligence roles.  Photograph: Andrew Harnik/Getty Images

blocks.text: Intelligence veterans criticised the appointments of Tulsi Gabbard as director of national intelligence and Kash Patel as director of the FBI, accusing both of lacking sufficient top-level experience in law enforcement.

For the 2026 financial year, funding requested for the principal agencies of the civilian intelligence community totalled $81bn. But the designation of criminal groups such as the Mexican drug cartels as foreign terrorist organisations has stretched resources.

An updated counter-terrorism strategy released in May by the Trump administration has been controversial. Many intelligence experts and analysts have highlighted how the strategy downplays the rising threat from rightwing extremism in the US and stresses instead the battle against leftwing violence, cartels and gangs.

“It is a very partial document [and] raises the question: are you protecting America or people who agree with you?” said Clarke. “We have finite resources now. You don’t have a blank cheque like after 9/11 and at the same time it’s not just Sunni jihadist groups which are considered the threat.”
after newsletter promotion

Devorah Margolin at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy said that the new strategy was a significant shift. “That is not to say that counter-terrorism policies cannot change as the landscape changes, but this year’s strategy appears more focused on a political agenda than the reality of the threat,” Margolin added.

blocks.caption: People in lower Manhattan watch smoke billow from the World Trade Center on 9/11. One expert said the focus has shifted from terrorism to threats from China and Russia.  Photograph: Amy Sancetta/AP

blocks.text: “While the strategy still acknowledged the threat posed by groups like the Islamic State and al-Qaida, it also expanded definitions of counter-terrorism. It sought to use the vast counter-terrorism bureaucracy that has been built over the last two decades for its own political agenda. This has spread dwindling counter-terrorism resources even thinner.”

The loss of experienced personnel is a significant problem, experts say, with many criticising the dismantlement last year of programmes aimed at countering extremist ideologies and preventing radicalisation.

Don Rassler, the director of strategic initiatives at the Combating Terrorism Center at West Point, said that terrorism became less of a priority as strategic focus shifted to real or potential threats from China and Russia, and warned the US needed to be careful the intelligence community did not “revert back to the dynamics that led to an event like 9/11”.

The 2001 attacks were the culmination of a series of attacks launched by Bin Laden on US targets. In 1996 and again in 1998, 10 years after founding al-Qaida, Bin Laden “declared war” on America with statements issued from a base in Afghanistan, listing grievances including US backing for “tyrannical, apostate” regimes in the Middle East such as in his native Saudi Arabia amid a broader diatribe against what he called western aggression against Muslims worldwide.

Shortly afterwards, double bombings demolished two US embassies in east Africa and a suicide attack nearly sank a US warship off Yemen in 2000. The failure of senior officials including George W Bush to act on multiple intelligence warnings was highlighted by the congressional investigation into the 9/11 attacks, as well as the failure of the FBI and the CIA to share with each other vital information that might have prevented the atrocity.

blocks.caption: The Freedom Tower rises above one of the 9/11 memorial reflecting pools. Photograph: Spencer Platt/Getty Images

blocks.text: An al-Qaida effort to blow up a passenger plane as it prepared to land in Detroit in 2009 was averted only at the last minute when explosives failed to detonate as intended. An attack a decade later by a single “self-radicalised” Saudi Arabian air force officer in Florida which killed three was linked to the organisation’s affiliate in Yemen.

Since then, there have been more than 100 attacks in the US by violent Islamic extremists linked to the broader “jihadi” movement, according to a count by the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
Rassler said extremist Islamist groups were still a key priority but with fewer resources and fewer people the US had “to accept more terrorist risk”.

“There hasn’t been another attack … but there is a danger of believing that the [terrorist] threat isn’t there. The threat is different in many ways from 10 years ago and we have to be as clear-eyed as possible about it.”

articles.title: DOJ's Vida 'saddened' Sara Duterte not feeling safe, says law agents ready to protect
articles.summary: Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida on Thursday assured that law enforcement agencies are ready to do their duty to protect all Filipinos, following Vice President Sara Duterte's remark that she did…

blocks.text: Published September 10, 2026 12:49pm

Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida on Thursday assured that law enforcement agencies are ready to do their duty to protect all Filipinos, following Vice President Sara Duterte's remark that she did not feel safe in the country.

"Nakakalungkot po na para sa pangalawang pinakamataas na opisyal ng ating bansa na ano… of course, these are legitimate feelings. I don't like to speculate where she is coming from," he said in a press briefing.
(It is sad that for the second-highest official of our country to, you know… of course, these are legitimate feelings. I don't like to speculate where she is coming from.)

"Nakakalungkot pero patuloy naman po pinapatotohanan ng ating iba't ibang law enforcement agencies na sila ay handa at gaganap sa kanilang tungkulin para ma-secure hindi lamang ang ating vice president, kundi lahat ng Pilipino," he added.
(It is sad, but our various law enforcement agencies continue to demonstrate that they are ready and will perform their duties to secure not only our vice president, but all Filipinos.)

To recall, the DOJ filed three counts of grave threats against the vice president over her remarks that she hired an individual to kill President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former speaker Martin Romualdez, should an alleged plot against her succeed.
Duterte posted bail before the Quezon City Regional Trial Court (RTC) on Saturday, a day after the issuance of an arrest warrant against her in connection to her grave threats case.
Moments before this, the vice president repeatedly said to the media and her lawyers that she did not feel safe.
Vida said the DOJ and its panel of prosecutors decided on the charges based on evidence.

"Ang panawagan po ng inyong lingkod, patungkol tayong magtiwala sa mga institusyon, sa mga proseso na nangyayari... mayroon pong mga karapatan ang bawat isa, mga akusado o respondent, ginagalang po natin 'yan," he said.
(We call on the public to trust the institutions and the processes that are taking place. Each one has rights, the accused or respondent, and we respect that.)
He also denied claims of "selective justice."
"Tayo po ay produkto ng ating ginawa. Kung may ginawa tayong labag sa batas, may kakaharapin tayo. Kasi mas mabigat po na hindi natin kaharapan 'yung consequences ng ating ginawa," he said.
(We are products of what we have done. If we did something against the law, we will face the consequences. Because it is heavier if we do not face the consequences of what we have done.)
Vida also reiterated the department's position that only the President is immune from suit while in office. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Russia outpacing Ukraine's air defences with daily use of new jet-powered drones
articles.summary: The new models can travel at speeds of up to 300mph, faster than Ukraine's air defence interceptors.

blocks.text: Russia fired its new rapid, jet-powered drones against Ukraine every day throughout August, BBC Verify analysis of Ukrainian Air Force data has found, escalating its use of a weapon that Kyiv's air defences are struggling to deal with.

It marked the first time that daily attacks by Moscow's new upgraded Geran drones were recorded in Ukrainian Air Force data. The growing use of jet-propelled and other varieties of drones prompted President Volodymyr Zelensky to condemn what he called an unfolding "horror" over the skies of Kyiv.

Ukraine's military recently told the BBC that jet-powered drone attacks grew from 350 in June to 1,600 in July and 2,800 in August. In five of the nightly attacks in August, these drones outnumbered the older, slower models.

"The reason for turning to jet-powered drones is that they are much faster than the previous generation and it makes it much more difficult for Ukraine to intercept them," said Dr Marina Miron, an expert on military technology at King's College London.

The upgraded munitions can cruise at more than 300mph, significantly faster than older models and well beyond the top speed of Kyiv's interceptors. The drones are powered by turbojet engines, some of which, according to Ukrainian military intelligence, are sourced from China.

According to Zelensky, the drones were used as part of a wave of attacks that killed at least 12 people and injured 20 more on 1 September. Six of the casualties were railway workers after a depot was hit in Kyiv.

Earlier this year Ukraine showed relative success in countering Russian drones and was intercepting 94% of long-range drones, according to Zelensky. But the speed of the newer drones has prompted the latest round in Kyiv and Moscow's arms race. On 10 August, Ukraine's deputy head of military intelligence, Maj Gen Vadym Skibitskyi, said his forces needed new interceptor missiles "capable of matching [jet-drones'] speed".

articles.title: King Harald V's funeral: Norway bids farewell as crowds, royals converge
articles.summary: OSLO, Norway — Norway bade its final farewell to Harald V on Wednesday as crowds lined the streets and foreign royals and leaders converged on Oslo for the funeral of the long-serving king, who was…

blocks.text: OSLO, Norway — Norway bade its final farewell to Harald V on Wednesday as crowds lined the streets and foreign royals and leaders converged on Oslo for the funeral of the long-serving king, who was remembered as a popular monarch with a down-to-earth touch.

A 21-gun salute rang out over the capital at the start of a funeral procession from the royal palace to Oslo Cathedral. Harald’s son, new King Haakon VIII, and other senior royals walked behind the coffin, draped with the red Norwegian royal standard. Harald’s widow, Queen Sonja, and Haakon’s wife, Queen Mette-Marit, followed in a car.
Norwegian officials and foreign dignitaries joined the solemn procession. They included the monarchs of Sweden, Denmark, Spain, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Monaco and Jordan.

Also present were the heir to the British throne, Prince William, and Japan’s Crown Prince Akishino, as well as political leaders from more than 20 countries, including Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Harald V was a king who met people ‘in his rubber boots’
As the funeral service began, Norway came to a halt for a minute of silence.

Harald, who died on Aug. 28 aged 89, was Europe’s oldest monarch and had reigned for 35 years. He modernized the royal house but refused to follow in the footsteps of other aging monarchs who recently abdicated. His son immediately became king and last week took an oath of allegiance to Norway’s constitution in parliament.
The parliament’s speaker, Masud Gharahkhani, said at the service that “King Harald was close to the people” and recalled that “he wasn’t afraid to meet people in his rubber boots.”
He remembered Harald saying in his 2008 New Year’s address: “I wish we would stop using the term ‘the weakest in society.’ In reality, some of these people are among the strongest of us all.”
“He lived up to his motto: He gave his all for Norway,” Gharahkhani said.
Large crowds lined the streets ahead of the funeral

Large crowds flocked to Oslo for the funeral, and thousands stood behind barriers on streets lined with national flags. The downtown area was closed to vehicles and electric scooters, and police had instructed people not to bring bicycles, umbrellas or sharp objects.

People tuned in across the country of about 5.6 million. Scores of churches, libraries, cultural centers and city halls made big screens available for the public to watch the funeral, public broadcaster NRK reported. The government said it wasn’t an official holiday, but schools and workplaces could individually opt to let students and employees watch.

Ahead of the funeral, Norwegians waited patiently to file past Harald’s coffin in the chapel of the royal palace. The queue was seven hours long at one point over the weekend. Over 46,000 people visited the chapel during the week it lay in state.

“The love between the people and King Harald has not ended — quite the contrary,” said Bishop Olav Fykse Tveit, who led the funeral service, pointing to the tributes left outside the palace after his death. “The sea of flowers, along with the words and drawings that accompany them, speaks loudly and clearly of a heart so full that it overflows.”

After the funeral, Harald’s coffin was taken in a smaller procession to Akershus Fortress, where his predecessors are buried in the crypt of the palace chapel. Haakon followed with the two other Scandinavian monarchs, King Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden and King Frederik X of Denmark.

Among those who attended the funeral was Mette-Marit’s eldest son and Haakon’s stepson, Marius Borg Høiby, who has no royal title or duties. Høiby is appealing against a rape conviction after a trial earlier this year that cast a shadow over the royal family.

Norway’s monarchy traces its origins to King Harald Fairhair in the ninth century. When Norway regained its independence from Sweden in 1905, three-quarters of voters in a national plebiscite approved restoring the monarchy.

The Norwegian royal house has kinfolk in other European royal families. Harald and Haakon are related to both Britain’s King Charles III and Spain’s King Felipe VI: They’re all descendants of the U.K.’s Queen Victoria, who reigned from 1837 until her death in 1901.

Today, the throne’s role is largely symbolic and power lies with the elected government and parliament, but the Norwegian royal family retains a role in promoting the wealthy Scandinavian nation around the world. /dl

articles.title: Jessica Pegula looks to thwart Sabalenka 3-peat in US Open semis
articles.summary: NEW YORK–Aryna Sabalenka is gunning for her third US Open title in a row — can Jessica Pegula stop her this time? The two meet on Thursday night as part of a blockbuster women’s…

blocks.text: FILE–Jessica Pegula of the US (R) is congratulated by Belarus’ Aryna Sabalenka after winning the women’s singles semi-final match at the WTA500 Berlin Tennis Open tournament in Berlin on June 20, 2026. Pegula wins 4-6, 7-6, 0-6. (Photo by John MACDOUGALL / AFP)
NEW YORK–Aryna Sabalenka is gunning for her third US Open title in a row — can Jessica Pegula stop her this time?
The two meet on Thursday night as part of a blockbuster women’s semi-final lineup that features all four top seeds — the first time since 1975 the top four women all made it so far in the event.
Third-seeded Pegula will face top-seeded Sabalenka for the third year in a row at Flushing Meadows, where she lost to the Belarusian in the 2024 final and in the semi-finals last year.
Since falling in the semis last year, Pegula has won two of three meetings with Sabalenka, and the 32-year-old American would like to transfer that success to the Grand Slam stage.

“I think it’s fun to look at the rivalry we’ve had. She’s gotten me here the last couple of years. I have been able to beat her a few times, maybe on a smaller stage, so I think that’s going to be kind of a hurdle for me to get over,” Pegula said as she prepared for the latest instalment of her rivalry with Sabalenka.
Thursday night’s other semi-final will feature second-seeded Australian Open champion Elena Rybakina taking on 2023 US Open winner Coco Gauff.
Rybakina, assured of supplanting Sabalenka atop the world rankings just by reaching the semis, is trying to stay focused on the hunt for third Grand Slam title.
“It’s a different achievement,” she said of reaching No. 1. “Mostly you think about the titles in the end of the day.”
AFP Sport looks at women’s semi-final action on Day 12 of the US Open:
Aryna Sabalenka (BLR x1) v Jessica Pegula (USA x3):

items: Sabalenka leads head to head 9-4

blocks.text: Pegula came into the tournament as one of three players with a chance to take the number one ranking from Sabalenka, but that discussion became moot when Rybakina reached the semis to be assured of ascending to the top spot.
For Sabalenka, that’s a side issue as she tries to become just the third woman after Chris Evert and Serena Williams to win three straight US Open titles.
“Three-peat, sounds great,” said Sabalenka, who was unable to complete the treble when she had the chance at the 2025 Australian Open.

“What I learned from Australia is it’s really important to shut down all of the noises and having that on the back of your mind,” Sabalenka said. “It’s nothing wrong about that, just as long as you’re focusing on yourself, as long as you’re ready to fight, basically.”
The Belarusian, who had hit the skids since winning her third title of the year at Miami in March, knows Pegula is a serious obstacle.
“I love playing against her because it’s a battle, because it’s a fight, and I love being under pressure and going through tough challenges. It’s going to be really high-intensity level of tennis.
