articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation"s (NBI) complaint against Batangas First District Representative Leandro Leviste and six others over the alleged plot against Executive Secretary Ralph Recto is…

blocks.text: Published September 10, 2026 11:40am

The National Bureau of Investigation’s (NBI) complaint against Batangas First District Representative Leandro Leviste and six others over the alleged plot against Executive Secretary Ralph Recto is currently being evaluated, Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida said Thursday.
Vida said the complaint may either be returned to the NBI or proceed to preliminary Investigation.

“Under the rules, we have 10 days to evaluate and to determine whether the case will proceed to its preliminary investigation or to dismiss the same and give it back to the NBI,” Vida said at a press briefing.
The secretary said the NBI’s recommendation to file qualified human trafficking charges against the respondents was filed on September 4.
Among the respondents are Leviste, former Negros Oriental congressman Jacinto Paras, four lawyers, and one individual.
To recall, NBI agents rescued several individuals during an entrapment operation.
Some of the victims later claimed that Paras allegedly told them they would be paid to create a story and sign an affidavit, and they would receive their payment in tranches as the case went on.

Leviste's camp previously denied involvement in the supposed ploy, while Paras' camp said the alleged talent manager approached them voluntarily to testify and asked for help in drafting the affidavit.
Meanwhile, Vida said they are also looking into the request to issue an Immigration Lookout Bulletin Order against the respondents. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: China fires flares at unarmed PH aircraft over Kalayaan Island Group
articles.summary: China fires flares at unarmed PH aircraft over Kalayaan Island Group

blocks.text: PCG SAYS
Published September 10, 2026 11:38am

The Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) on Thursday said Chinese forces fired multiple flares at an unarmed PCG aircraft conducting a routine maritime domain awareness (MDA) flight over the Kalayaan Island Group (KIG) in the West Philippine Sea (WPS) on Monday.
PCG spokesperson for the WPS Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela said the Philippine aircraft was challenged over the radio by Chinese forces occupying Zamora (Subi) Reef before it landed on Pag-asa Island.

“The PCG recorded multiple flare discharges by the People's Liberation Army (PLA) against an unarmed PCG aircraft conducting a legitimate MDA flight over the KIG on 07 September 2026,” he said in a statement.

“Prior to landing on Pag-asa Island, the PCG aircraft was challenged over radio by Chinese forces illegally occupying Zamora (Subi) Reef, which then fired flares in its direction. Chinese forces illegally occupying Panganiban (Mischief) Reef repeated the same actions,” he added.
GMA News Onlight has sought comment from the Chinese Embassy in Manila about the incident but it has yet to provide a statement as of posting time.
Chinese maritime militia vessels were also seen inside the lagoons of Subi and Mischief Reefs, according to Tarriela.
No personnel were seen on the decks of the vessels or on the reclaimed facilities, while no vehicular movement was monitored on the artificial islands, he added.
PCG chief Admiral Ronnie Gil Gavan said, “Flares were fired at an unarmed Coast Guard aircraft. The PCG does not need to characterize this behavior."
He cited the 2016 arbitral ruling, which stated that Mischief Reef is a low-tide elevation forming part of the Philippines' exclusive economic zone (EEZ) and continental shelf.
Gavan said China's reclamation activities at the feature were conducted in violation of Philippine sovereign rights.

The PCG said the discharge of flares against an aircraft in flight also endangered flight safety and disregarded China's obligation to exercise due regard under the Convention on International Civil Aviation.

“The PCG will continue to conduct MDA flights over the West Philippine Sea undeterred, and will continue to document and expose China's aggression and violations of international law,” the PCG said. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Elena Rybakina secures No. 1 ranking, eyes more Grand Slam glory
articles.summary: NEW YORK–Elena Rybakina will rise to number one in the world rankings for the first time after reaching the US Open semi-finals, but for the Kazakh star the chance at a third Grand Slam title remains…

blocks.text: Elena Rybakina, of Kazakhstan, celebrates winning a match against Qinwen Zheng, of China, during the quarterfinal round of the U.S. Open tennis championships, Wednesday, Sept. 9, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Seth Wenig)

NEW YORK–Elena Rybakina will rise to number one in the world rankings for the first time after reaching the US Open semi-finals, but for the Kazakh star the chance at a third Grand Slam title remains her most pressing concern.

“It means a lot, of course,” Rybakina said after rallying to beat Paris Olympics gold medallst Zheng Qinwen in three sets in the quarter-finals to ensure she’ll supplant Aryna Sabalenka at the summit.
“It’s a great achievement, and I feel like you will appreciate and think about it even more when you finish your career,” Rybakina said.
“Now, you still need to keep on going. I want to win the titles still in the tournaments, so all my thoughts are just for the next match.”
That will be against fourth-seeded former champion Coco Gauff.
Rybakina knows that such opportunities can be few and far between. She won her second career Grand Slam title at the Australian Open in January, four years after capturing her first at Wimbledon.
She’s especially grateful to have put herself so close to another major after a heel injury forced her out of the WTA tournament in Cincinnati last month.
Unable to walk without pain for several days, she’s had to cautiously manage her training, rest and treatment.
“It was not ideal, and I was stressed, of course,” Rybakina said as the tournament got underway, but she progressed through the first four rounds without dropping a set.

Now she’s two wins away from her third major title, posting impressive wins along the way over four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka and Yuliia Starodubtseva — who beat her in the second round at the French Open.

Even her slow start against Zheng had its encouraging side. Rybakina, who had been 0-6 in prior US Open matches in which she dropped the first set, was pleased she was able to shake off distractions and discomfort with the awkwardly shaded court and mount a comeback.
“Very difficult match, very stressful,” she said. “A lot of thoughts going through the head in the beginning but glad that I managed to find a way.”

blocks.text: September 10, 2026 | 11:32am

Rep. Martin Romualdez (Leyte) lies in a hospital bed at Cardinal Santos Medical Center as police place him under custody on Sept. 7, 2026, following the Sandiganbayan's issuance of a warrant in a P7.44-billion plunder case.
Philstar.com / Contributed photo

MANILA, Philippines — Former House Speaker Martin Romaldez is set to be detained at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas after the Sandiganbayan Third Division ordered his transfer to the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) on Thursday, September 10.

“We hereby commit to you the living person of accused Ferdinand Martin Gomez Romualdez, who is charged in the aforesaid case for the crime of plunder, to be held therein as a detention prisoner,” the order read.
This is the same jail facility where Sens. Rodante Marcoleta, Jinggoy Estrada and former lawmaker Mike Defensor are also detained for plunder charges.
His arraignment is scheduled on September 14 at 8:30 a.m.
The commitment order was issued as the court heard the Leyte lawmaker’s motion for continued hospital arrest.

Philippine National Police Spokesperson Allan Rae Co earlier said in an interview with GMA’s Unang Balita that Romualdez will not be able to attend the hearing as doctors said he was “medically unfit to travel."

Romualdez is asking the court to allow him to remain confined at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City, saying he is suffering from multiple illnesses like heart-related diseases, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia and primary hypothyroidism.
The Ombudsman, however, earlier said that they will oppose the request for continued confinement at Cardinal Santos.
Authorities are asking the court to transfer Romualdez to the Philippine National Police General Hospital in Camp Crame.
Romualdez is facing a P7.44-billion non-bailable plunder charge linked to the flood control corruption scandal.

articles.title: Trump offers $5,000 to every American if Republicans win midterm elections
articles.summary: With approximately 270 million US adults, the idea would cost around $1.35 trillion

items: President Trump proposed a $5,000 'Trump dividend' for every American adult if Republicans retain control of Congress, a move aimed at persuading voters ahead of the midterm elections.

The convention in Dallas highlighted Trump's central role in the Republican Party, despite his declining popularity and the challenges faced by some Republican candidates who may need to distance themselves from him.

Speakers at the event focused on attacking Democrats and their policies, while key voter concerns like the Iran war and cost of living received less attention, raising questions about the effectiveness of Trump's strategy.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

DALLAS, USA – US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday, September 9, he would pay every American adult a $5,000 “Trump dividend” if Republicans retain control of Congress in November’s midterm election, a striking attempt to persuade voters to back his party.

Trump made the proposal at his Republican Party’s first-ever midterm convention, but it was not immediately clear how the payments would work or whether they would be legal. With approximately 270 million US adults, the idea would cost around $1.35 trillion.

During his primetime address, Trump boasted of completing “the greatest two years in the history of the presidency,” putting himself squarely at the center of the election despite his deepening unpopularity.

But it was not clear whether his campaign-style speech would appeal to the critical swing voters who opinion polls show have drifted away from Trump’s party, amid growing dissatisfaction with the cost of living and the war on Iran.

“We hand America’s future to the radical left Democrats, and our nation will spend the next decade just getting back on its feet,” he said. “Vote Republicans and we will leave the world in our dust for generations to come.”

The two-day Dallas gathering, where Trump will also deliver the closing remarks on Thursday, September 10, after Vice President JD Vance’s keynote address, underscores the extent to which Republicans’ fortunes are tethered to Trump and serves as a showcase for their strategy ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
The event was so centered on the president that Republican national committee chairman Joe Gruters informally dubbed it “Trumpapalooza,” a nod to the popular Lollapalooza music festival.

The focus on Trump amounts to a risky bet that he can mobilize the voters who carried him to the presidency two years ago, despite public polls showing his approval ratings have hit an all-time low. The president vowed to pay multiple visits to battleground states and districts in the eight weeks until Election Day.
“I’m asking you to pretend that I’m on the ballot,” Trump said, a line that may have pleased Democratic campaign strategists just as much as MAGA voters.

The convention presented a tough choice in particular for Republicans facing difficult elections who may need to distance themselves from the president to broaden their appeal but cannot afford to alienate Trump’s most committed supporters.

Many such Republicans skipped the convention, including Representative Tom Barrett of Michigan, Senator Dan Sullivan of Alaska and Senator Susan Collins of Maine, all facing strong Democratic challengers this fall.

Some, however, elected to travel to Dallas. At least 16 candidates in competitive House and Senate races were scheduled to speak, according to the RNC schedule. Among those who spoke on Wednesday were Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, a close Trump ally who is locked in a tough Senate race with Democratic lawmaker James Talarico, and Ohio Senator Jon Husted, who faces former Senator Sherrod Brown.
Though Trump insisted the 21,000-seat arena was “packed,” the upper sections remained largely empty during his speech capping Wednesday’s program.

While Republican officials had described the convention as an opportunity to tout Trump’s policies, most of the early speakers focused largely on attacking Democrats as extreme on topics such as transgender women in sports and border security – political red meat for the base.
Issues that voters have consistently cited as top concerns, the Iran war and the cost of living, received comparatively less attention.
Alabama state Representative Ernie Yarbrough, a convention attendee, said Trump needs to give voters a clearer sense of how long the war in Iran could last and what the administration’s aims are.
“People want to feel like we’re not getting stuck in an endless cycle,” he said.

Trump defended his decision to attack Tehran, saying he acted to prevent Iran from developing a nuclear weapon. He also promised that oil prices would drop “as soon as we win the war with Iran,” which he vowed would happen soon.

But the conflict shows little sign of ending more than six months after the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, and analysts have said Iran’s nuclear program has not been eliminated. Iran denies seeking a nuclear weapon.

blocks.caption: Trump advisers warn Iran conflict may last through end of his term, WSJ reports

blocks.text: Before Trump took the stage, a parade of speakers called Democrats “socialists” and “communists,” echoing one of Trump’s favorite attack lines following a handful of victories by democratic socialists in Democratic primary elections.
Democrats are “dangerous, radical and weird,” said Senator Tim Scott of South Carolina, the chairman of the party’s Senate campaign arm.

Wednesday’s program also featured a surprise pretaped video from Democratic US Senator John Fetterman, who introduced his fellow senator from Pennsylvania, Republican Dave McCormick, as his “great friend” while declaring he would work with Trump to protect the state’s steel industry.

Fetterman’s extraordinary participation appeared likely to emphasize the ideological divides plaguing the Democratic Party ahead of the midterms. Fetterman, who has increasingly clashed with left-wing Democrats, has denied speculation that he may leave the party.

The convention’s stakes are high for both parties. With the elections less than two months away, Republicans face the prospect of losing control of at least one chamber of Congress, with public polling showing Democrats more motivated to vote and Trump’s approval ratings deeply underwater.
The event faced stiff competition for viewers with the start of the NFL season, with opening night coinciding with a Super Bowl rematch between the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks.

Still, after months of negative headlines over the Iran war and inflation, many Republicans see the gathering as their best chance to promote candidates, draw contrasts with Democrats and energize a Republican electorate expressing less enthusiasm about voting than Democrats, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Sara Duterte trial barely registers in BARMM campaigns as election nears
articles.summary: Sara Duterte remains popular in the Muslim-majority region, as she does in many parts of Mindanao, yet her ongoing impeachment trial has barely figured in the campaign for seats in the Bangsamoro…

items: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has become a significant political issue in the Philippines, yet politicians in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region are largely avoiding the topic ahead of the upcoming parliamentary elections.

Candidates and political parties in BARMM are choosing to remain neutral, with many waiting to see the outcome of the impeachment before taking a stance, reflecting a cautious approach to political alignment.

Despite Duterte's popularity in the region, the impeachment trial is not expected to influence the election outcomes, as local political dynamics and alliances often take precedence over national issues.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

CAGAYAN DE ORO, Philippines – The ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has become one of the country’s biggest political showdowns, but in the Bangsamoro, where voters head to the polls next week, it appears to have become something many of its politicians would rather not talk about.

With Duterte still retaining a relatively strong national following and the impeachment proceedings putting her at odds with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and groups seeking her removal, politicians and political parties in the Bangsamoro region have largely avoided making the trial an issue in the region’s first parliamentary election, set for Monday, September 14.

Instead, candidates and political operators have mostly kept their options open, content to watch from the sidelines as the impeachment trial and the fight between the pro- and anti-Duterte camps unfold, at least until the votes are counted.
“Not much on the politicians, parang playing safe sila (it seems they are playing safe),” said Drieza Lininding, chairman of the Lanao del Sur-based Moro Consensus Group (MCG).
He said that some, like Lanao del Sur 1st District Representative Zia Adiong, are outspoken Duterte critics, “but many tend to wait and see how the impeachment will turn out.”

Adiong, a spokesman for the prosecution team in Duterte’s impeachment trial, is one of the more prominent exceptions. But his position has not necessarily translated into a broader political alignment in his province, including Marawi City, and across the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

The congressman is not running for a post in the BARMM regional government but his nephew Abdul Raul is seeking a seat in Lanao del Sur’s 3rd District, while another Adiong, Rashdi, is campaigning for a similar position in the 9th District.

The Adiongs, who supported what became the successful presidential bid of Marcos in 2022, have fielded candidates in the various parliamentary districts in Lanao del Sur and elsewhere in the BARMM through the Serbisyong Inklusibo-Alyansang Progresibo Party (SIAP).
Rappler sought comment from Adiong and three other politicians from competing political parties in the BARMM on Wednesday, September 9. None responded by the time of posting.
For Lininding, the bigger question may come after the September 14 vote.
If political forces aligned with Marcos lose, he said, some could blame the president and subsequently look to Duterte.
“The losing parties might blame PBBM (Marcos) and lean on VP Sara to exact political revenge,” Lininding said.

That suggests political fights at the national level do not necessarily dictate political choices in BARMM. It remains to be seen, but past elections have shown that predominantly Muslim areas in Mindanao are not politically uniform, and Duterte’s popularity may not automatically translate to votes for candidates in the parliamentary election.

Liezl Bugtay, deputy executive director of Climate Conflict Action Asia (CCAA), said the ongoing impeachment trial appears to have largely been absent from political discussions among voters, candidates, and parties in the BARMM.
“The ongoing impeachment trial won’t likely factor in the outcome of the BARMM elections,” Bugtay told Rappler. “It seems like it’s a non-issue in the region at this time.”

Candidates, she said, have generally not been tackling the impeachment in their campaign sorties, while voters appear to regard Duterte’s trial as separate from the election of the Bangsamoro parliament.
That distinction matters because the BARMM election is taking place against a political history in which national alliances have not always mapped neatly onto regional loyalties.
The political fault lines in the Bangsamoro looked different in 2022.

The contrast was striking. Take, for instance, Abdulraof Macacua, then a senior BARMM minister and head of the MILF’s armed wing, who is said to have backed Marcos in the 2022 elections. Yet his superior at the time and predecessor, then-interim chief minister Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim, openly supported former vice president Leni Robredo.
When the votes were counted, Murad and the MILF’s open endorsement did not translate to a Robredo victory. Marcos won with more than one million votes in the BARMM, more than twice Robredo’s total.
Duterte, Marcos’ running mate in 2022, also won in the BARMM by a landslide, including Sulu, which was then still part of the region.
The lesson from the upcoming election may not be that Duterte’s popularity is irrelevant. Rather, her popularity alone may not determine how BARMM voters cast their ballots on Monday.

Traditional politicians in the region have often aligned themselves with the administration in power. Many of those political networks remain focused on local alliances, family interests, and access to government resources rather than political battles playing out hundreds of kilometers away in Manila.
Still, the Duterte factor endures.
Lininding said many Meranaw in Lanao del Sur openly support Duterte, a sentiment he sees in many online political discussions.
He also pointed to Senator Robinhood Padilla, a hard-line Duterte supporter and the Senate’s only Muslim member.

Padilla’s political prominence gives the Duterte camp a foothold among Muslim voters in the national legislature. A former convict who converted to Islam and was granted an absolute pardon during the presidency of Sara’s father, Rodrigo Duterte, Padilla became the first Muslim senator since the late Santanina Rasul, who left office in 1995 after becoming the first Muslim woman elected to the Philippine Senate in 1987.

The disconnect is striking given that Sara Duterte remains popular in the Muslim-majority region, as she does in many parts of Mindanao, yet her ongoing impeachment trial has barely figured in the campaign for seats in the Bangsamoro parliament.
That could change, however, after the votes are counted next week.
Monday’s election will be the first parliamentary contest since the Bangsamoro region was created in 2019, determining who controls the legislature and who becomes its first elected chief minister.
But, for now, BARMM’s politicians and parties appear less interested in taking sides in the battle over the vice president’s fate than in ensuring their own political survival. – Rappler.com

items: Senators Alan Peter Cayetano and Pia Cayetano have left the Philippines, confirmed by the Bureau of Immigration, with no legal restrictions preventing their departure.

Their departure coincides with an investigation by the National Bureau of Investigation into alleged irregularities related to the Philippines' hosting of the 2019 Southeast Asian Games, where Alan Cayetano served as chairperson or the organizing committee.

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian stated that senators do not need to seek travel authority for personal trips, while Senator Panfilo Lacson expressed that the departure should not be a concern at this time.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Senators Alan Peter Cayetano and Pia Cayetano have left the Philippines, the Bureau of Immigration (BI) confirmed Thursday, September 10.

The BI’s confirmation came amid photos posted on social media showing the Cayetano siblings arriving in Singapore on Wednesday evening, September 9. A separate social media post also alleged that Taguig Mayor Lani Cayetano, Alan’s wife, flew to Singapore early Thursday.
“Based on BI records, there were no hold departure orders or derogatory records against the two senators, as of departure date, that would legally prevent them from leaving the country,” the BI said.
The agency declined to provide details about their travel, including their itinerary and other related information, citing the Data Privacy Act of 2012.

The Cayetanos’ departure comes as the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) prepares to recommend to the Department of Justice the filing of cases over alleged irregularities in the Philippines’ hosting of the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games.

Alan served as chairperson of the Philippine Southeast Asian Games Organizing Committee (PHISGOC), the nonprofit organization tasked with organizing and managing the country’s hosting of the 2019 SEA Games. He was also House speaker at the time.

NBI Director Melvin Matibag, however, said Cayetano was not identified as PHISGOC chairperson in the organization’s corporate records and financial documents, and the lack of a paper trail linking the senator to the alleged irregularities has hampered the investigation.
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian did not confirm the Cayetanos’ trip but said senators traveling abroad for personal reasons are not required to seek travel authority.
“Kapag personal trips, hindi na kailangan mag-abiso ang mga senador,” Gatchalian said. (Senators do not need to seek travel authority for personal trips.)

Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson, meanwhile, said the Cayetanos’ departure was not an issue at this point. He also urged the public to allow Alan to “take a break from the stress caused by issues that he himself created.”
“If it’s simply health-related, I sincerely wish him well despite our animosities,” said Lacson.

In July, Lacson submitted evidence on alleged irregularities in flood control projects in Taguig City to the Office of the Ombudsman for review. The allegations involved projects linked to Alan, who had denied the claims.

The departure of the Cayetanos from the country brings to three the total number of senators who are currently abroad. Senator Loren Legarda is on extended medical leave in France until September 16. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano and his sister, Sen. Pia Cayetano, both traveled out of the country, the Bureau of Immigration (BI) confirmed on Thursday.
The two were reportedly spotted boarding a flight to Singapore and arriving at Changi Airport a few hours later on Wednesday evening.
“The Bureau of Immigration (BI) confirms that Senators Alan Peter Cayetano and Pia Cayetano are currently out of the country,” the BI said in a statement.
It added: “Based on BI records, there were no hold departure orders or derogatory records against the two senators, as of departure date, that would legally prevent them from leaving the country.”

The Office of the Ombudsman previously ordered Alan Cayetano, along with Sen. Robin Padilla, to respond to obstruction of justice charges over their alleged involvement in assisting fugitive-at-large Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa in going into hiding.
Dela Rosa is facing a crime against humanity charge before the International Criminal Court for his alleged role in the drug war, but his arrest warrant has yet to be served as he remains in hiding.

The Ombudsman has likewise received evidence regarding supposed “ghost” infrastructure and reclamation projects in Taguig, some of which were reportedly inserted into the budget by Cayetano himself. /dl

articles.title: PNP continues hunt for Dela Rosa amid talks with alleged protectors
articles.summary: The Philippine National Police (PNP) said its efforts to arrest Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa remain ongoing despite reported negotiations with individuals allegedly protecting him.

blocks.text: Published September 10, 2026 10:58am
The Philippine National Police (PNP) said its efforts to arrest Senator Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa remain ongoing despite reported negotiations with individuals allegedly protecting him.

PNP spokesperson Police Colonel Allen Rae Co said authorities cannot disclose details of the negotiations or their operations, as this could pose risks to their mission, police personnel, and concerned individuals.

"Operational details cannot be publicly discussed as this will compromise our ongoing operations and could pose danger to the safety of everyone involved, not just our personnel but everyone involved," Co said at a press briefing on Wednesday.
"What we can confirm is that our efforts are ongoing and relentless. We will not yield and we will not be distracted from our goal," he added.
The PNP said individuals who assist Dela Rosa could also face legal consequences. The possible liability of the alleged protectors would depend on the nature of their cooperation.
The International Criminal Court (ICC) has issued a warrant of arrest for Dela Rosa in connection with the crimes against humanity case involving former President Rodrigo Duterte.
Rae confirmed that Dela Rosa is still in the Philippines. According to him, the senator is considered a flight risk.
The PNP said it is also pursuing the recovery of firearms registered to Dela Rosa.
Of the 117 registered firearms linked to Dela Rosa, 20 were surrendered in Davao Region while six were surrendered in Calabarzon, leaving 91 firearms still unaccounted for, according to Rae.
The PNP Firearms and Explosives Office (FEO) is coordinating with Dela Rosa's family for the surrender of the remaining firearms. — VDV, GMA News

It issued the remark amid reports that the Cayetanos boarded a flight on Wednesday.
GMA News Online has sought their camps’ comment and will publish their response once available. —VAL, GMA News

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano and his sister, Sen. Pia Cayetano, both traveled out of the country, the Bureau of Immigration (BI) confirmed on Thursday.

The Office of the Ombudsman previously ordered Alan Cayetano, along with Sen. Robin Padilla, to respond to obstruction of justice charges over their alleged involvement in assisting fugitive-at-large Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa in going into hiding.
Dela Rosa is facing a crime against humanity charge before the International Criminal Court for his alleged role in the drug war, but his arrest warrant has yet to be served as he remains in hiding.

articles.title: Bhutan’s 1st ramen shop thrives despite high-altitude challenges
articles.summary: At 2,300 meters above sea level in the Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan, making an authentic bowl of Japanese ramen presented an unexpected problem: the water boiled too soon. But after years of…

blocks.text: At 2,300 meters above sea level in the Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan, making an authentic bowl of Japanese ramen presented an unexpected problem: the water boiled too soon.

But after years of experimentation, Bhutanese owner Tshering and his Japanese wife, Sayaka Sakurai, have turned Hayate Ramen, the country’s first ramen restaurant, into a popular fixture in the capital Thimphu as it marks its 10th anniversary this year.
The 74-seat restaurant now serves around 150 bowls of ramen a day, with lines sometimes forming at lunchtime. Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay has been a customer since before taking office.

The 48-year-old business owner previously worked as a driver and auto mechanic for a travel agency. He met Sakurai, 50, when she visited Bhutan with her mother around 2006 or 2007, and the couple married in 2009.

They moved in 2010 to Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture, near Sakurai’s hometown of Sakuragawa. Tshering taught himself Japanese, worked at an auto factory and developed a passion for ramen as the couple explored the city’s many ramen shops.
“Tshering fell in love with ramen,” Sakurai said. “During the six and a half years we lived together in Japan, I think he ate it almost every day.”
Eventually, eating ramen was not enough. Tshering took a part-time job at a ramen shop and began thinking about what he could take back to his homeland.
He initially considered returning to the auto industry before realizing that ramen could work in Bhutan if adapted to local tastes, given the country’s fondness for chili peppers.
“I wanted to go back to Bhutan someday, but I wondered what I could bring back with me,” he said.
Tshering began studying the business and enrolled in a five-day course at the Yamato Ramen School in Kagawa Prefecture, learning noodle and soup preparation, toppings and restaurant management.
“If I hadn’t gone to that school, I wouldn’t be where I am today,” he said. “It was a turning point in my life.”
The couple poured their savings into the venture, supplemented by crowdfunding, and flew to Bhutan on one-way tickets.
Hayate Ramen opened in November 2016. But Thimphu’s altitude quickly complicated Tshering’s efforts to reproduce the ramen he had learned to make in Japan.

Water boils at a temperature about 5 C lower than in lowland Japan, making it difficult to achieve the richness he wanted in the soup. Tshering experimented with simmering times, noodle recipes and the composition of the local soft water until he found a formula that worked.
The workload was relentless. Tshering began his days at 2 a.m. preparing soup, while Sakurai sometimes slept beside the noodle-making machine because there was no time to return home.
Customers were initially scarce. On some days, sales were just 2,000 ngultrum ($21), equivalent to around five bowls at current prices.

“The first year was really tough, and the stress kept building,” Sakurai said. “Some staff would simply stop coming to work without telling us. I wondered how long we could carry on, but we didn’t even have enough money for a flight home.”

Still, they refused to compromise on quality, sourcing ingredients locally where possible and making some toppings themselves. Suppliers were initially puzzled when they requested pork bones rather than meat for their tonkotsu ramen.

Word gradually spread about the restaurant’s consistent quality and quick service. As smartphones gave Bhutanese consumers greater exposure to Japanese food, customers also began requesting dishes such as karaage fried chicken and sushi rolls.
The couple responded by expanding the menu, adding tsukemen dipping noodles, curry rice and agedashi tofu, as well as beef, chicken, pork and vegetarian choices.
“If families or groups of friends come and there isn’t something everyone can eat, they’ll go somewhere else,” Sakurai said. “Offering people what they want is one reason we’ve lasted 10 years.”

Around 80 percent of customers are now Bhutanese, with some traveling from towns and villages outside Thimphu specifically to eat ramen. Tshering said many first encountered the dish through Japanese manga.
Some of the restaurant’s biggest fans are children.
“If the children come, the adults come too,” Tshering said with a laugh. “Sometimes children walk past the shop and start crying because they want ramen.”
For Sakurai, who previously worked as a nurse, the transformation remains difficult to comprehend.

“When I look at the restaurant and every seat is taken, I still sometimes wonder if I’m dreaming,” she said. “When I look back over these 10 years, so many people’s faces come to mind. It makes me think how interesting life can be.”
The couple named their restaurant Hayate, meaning a fresh breeze, to reflect their hope of bringing something new to Bhutan.
A decade later, they are still finding ways to keep that breeze blowing. /dl

articles.title: Trump’s Qatari Air Force One delayed after evacuation slide deployed
articles.summary: JOINT BASE ANDREWS, United States — US President Donald Trump’s Qatari-gifted Air Force One was delayed on the tarmac Wednesday after an emergency inflatable slide accidentally deployed,…

blocks.text: JOINT BASE ANDREWS, United States — US President Donald Trump’s Qatari-gifted Air Force One was delayed on the tarmac Wednesday after an emergency inflatable slide accidentally deployed, raising fresh questions over the safety of the jet.
Trump — who was preparing to travel to a Republican Party convention in Dallas from Joint Base Andrews — had to wait in his helicopter before being able to board the plane following the incident.
The 80-year-old then told reporters that inspectors were checking one of the Boeing 747’s inflatable slides used for emergency evacuations.
“They’re checking the slide over here, and I think it’s going to take 15 minutes,” Trump said on the tarmac before boarding.
But a person briefed on the situation later told AFP that “military personnel accidentally triggered the slide.”

The plane’s safety has been the subject of recurring questions, and the issue came to a head during a recent dramatic incident in Turkey, where Trump secretly switched to a different aircraft amid security concerns.
Asked by an AFP reporter Wednesday whether Trump was sure the jet was safe, Trump responded: “Yeah I am, or I wouldn’t be on it.”

Upon arrival at Joint Base Andrews near Washington, Trump remained on his helicopter for an unusually long time before finally boarding Air Force One, the name given to an airplane carrying the US head of state.

This gave reporters time to observe an inflatable slide deployed on the right side of the jet, as well as the former presidential plane being repositioned from its hangar onto the tarmac, with its boarding bridges extended.
The current Air Force One eventually took off and landed in Texas, where Trump is to speak at a Republican convention in a bid to rally his party ahead of November’s midterm elections.

“As the president has said, the slide was checked out to make sure everything works perfectly,” White House Communications Director Steven Cheung said in a statement to AFP, adding that Trump would “deliver his much-anticipated speech to a raucous and sold-out crowd.”
Security

The Qatari plane, repainted in a red, white and blue livery chosen by Trump, was last in the spotlight in July, when Trump decided at the last minute not to join press and top administration members on the jet leaving the NATO summit in Turkey.
Trump pretended to board the old Air Force One as planned — only to secretly deplane from a different door, into a catering truck that took him to a third plane.
The move was in response to a reported security threat from Iran involving a surface-to-air missile.
Trump recently announced that work to enhance security measures on the new jet would begin in October and take two months — a month longer than he had previously said.

The Qatari royal family donated the luxurious jet last year after Trump complained about the condition of the two older Air Force One aircraft, which feature a distinctive white, silver and robin’s egg blue color scheme and have been in service since 1990.
The donated plane, valued at several hundred million dollars, has raised major ethical and constitutional questions regarding gifts a US president may receive from foreign governments.
But it also raised questions about the security of military equipment given by a foreign power.
The jet has already been refitted by the military, and is to be used until Boeing delivers two new aircraft in the coming years.
Trump has indicated that he intends to keep the Qatari plane for his future presidential museum. /dl

articles.title: Trump takes center stage as Republicans fight midterm tide
articles.summary: DALLAS, United States — A defiant Donald Trump vowed Republicans would “surge forward” in November’s midterms Wednesday, seeking to rally his party against grim election…

blocks.text: DALLAS, United States — A defiant Donald Trump vowed Republicans would “surge forward” in November’s midterms Wednesday, seeking to rally his party against grim election forecasts, weak approval ratings and mounting voter discontent over prices and his war with Iran.
The president took the stage at an extraordinary Republican midterm convention in Dallas built around persuading his supporters that he is effectively on the ballot on November 3.
“In 55 days, Americans will be going to the polls in one of the most important elections in our country’s history,” Trump told the crowd.
“Your vote will decide whether our country stumbles at the starting gate of the next 250 years or surges forward and never ever looks back.”
Decision Desk HQ projects Democrats to win the House 230-205 and the Senate to finish 51-49 in their favor in November.
Trump, whose approval rating has fallen into the low 30s in recent polling, used his keynote speech to argue that Republican fortunes remain tied to his presidency.

The president is due to return for the convention finale Thursday, after a keynote address from Vice President JD Vance. Cabinet members, congressional leaders and candidates in closely watched House and Senate races are also on the program.

The central Republican gamble is that Trump can mobilize voters personally loyal to him without further alienating independents who have soured on his presidency amid inflation woes, gasoline prices topping $4 a gallon and the continuing war with Iran.
“I’m asking you to pretend that I’m on the ballot — I’m on the ballot, I’m on the ballot — just one more time,” he said.
“Because if we lose, you’re going to lose your border, you’re going to lose your tax cuts, you’re going to lose your safety and security.”
Inside the American Airlines Center, there was little sign of Republican anxiety about November.
The convention even featured a video address from Democratic Senator John Fetterman, who has become increasingly at odds with his party’s left wing over issues including Israel.
His appearance intensified speculation about his political future, although Fetterman has said he has no intention of switching parties.
Republicans highlighted tax cuts and immigration enforcement, touting boosted manufacturing and lower prescription drug prices.
One of the main talking points was the danger of empowering what speakers characterized as a dangerously far-left Democratic Party.
“There is a crazy little sick cloud over our country,” Trump said. “We will defeat communism in America and vote for American freedom.”
Political headwinds
The cavernous arena was festooned with Trump posters as supporters milled around in sequined jackets patterned with his name, image and the American flag, some topped with ten-gallon hats.

Food stalls hawked overpriced snacks while merchandise stands did brisk business in T-shirts, mugs, posters and copies of the latest literary offering from the Trump clan, “Under Siege” by the president’s second son, Eric.

Despite the political headwinds facing Republicans, the mood was festive. Chants of “USA! USA!” — familiar from Trump’s campaign rallies — echoed around the hall as the national anthem opened the program.
Susan Kokinda, 77, a conservative podcaster who traveled to the gathering from Michigan, told AFP she expected Republicans to “do just fine” in November.
“The conventional wisdom is the party in power loses. But I always say Donald Trump is not a conventional president, and he’s reshaping the Republican Party,” she said.
The gathering is the first Republican national convention held specifically for a midterm election, although no candidates are being nominated and no formal party business is planned.
Instead, organizers have constructed what amounts to a two-night television rally touting Trump’s record and Republican candidates.
More than 100 House members and candidates were expected, with over 50 speakers or presentations scheduled each night.
Trump’s national television showcase faces an unusually formidable rival, however: both convention nights coincide with the opening games of the NFL season. /dl

articles.title: Instagram boss says users will be ‘overwhelmed’ with brand content in algorithm-free world
articles.summary:
Adam Mosseri says platform’s algorithm ‘feels like a black box’ but company trying to give users more control after Labor announces opt-out plan

Instagram’s chief executive has said users…

blocks.text: Instagram’s chief executive has said users will have a worse experience in an algorithm-free world, seeing more brand-related content, and spend less time on the app.

The comments come as the Australian government plans to give users the option to opt out of algorithms, with the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, announcing plans on Tuesday to require social media platforms to prompt users to choose between a feed of algorithm-recommended content or a reverse chronological feed of the pages users follow. Labor also plans to introduce a range of measures designed to address online harm on the sites.

In a briefing with journalists on Thursday to launch the company’s Algo Confessions series in Australia, Instagram’s chief executive, Adam Mosseri, did not comment directly on the Albanese government proposal but said Instagram had a range of algorithms in operation. Those include ranking which friends’ stories you see more often, or which users come up first in message suggestions based on interactions, as well as the algorithm that determines the content people see in their feeds.

The launch of the series in Australia is the first outside the US. It features celebrities and influencers detailing how Instagram determines what content ends up in a user’s feed, and how the user can have some control over that by adding or removing tags in their settings.
Mosseri said just a “very vocal minority” wants social media to go back to reverse chronological feeds, which he said would just incentivise people to post more.
“What ends up happening is the best way to get more reach is just to post more often and those who can afford to post the most often do and then therefore get the most reach,” he said.
“And it turns out your friends post a lot less than creators, who post a lot less than brands and companies.”
He said people would be “overwhelmed” with content from brands, and creators and friends would be drowned out.

“What happens is people become a bit less interested in the experience and they use it a lot less, which then means that there’s less reach to go around and people start to get more and more mad about the fact that their reach is going down because the overall pie gets smaller.”
He said engagement and user satisfaction goes down.
“It’s this interesting tension between what an individual might want and what happens when you actually explode that to the entire community,” he said.

“That’s not to say that ranking is perfect, it’s not, we make mistakes – one of the things that frustrates me about ranking is that we end up over-optimising for things that we can measure and undervaluing things that are more difficult to measure.”
after newsletter promotion
Mosseri said Instagram’s ranking algorithm “feels like a black box” but was something Instagram was trying to give users more control over by opting out of certain topics in their recommendations.
He said in the future, Meta’s AI models could eventually allow users to talk to the app to understand why they are seeing certain types of content.
Mosseri said he did not believe the app to be the clinical definition of “addictive”.

“I don’t believe Instagram is addictive – I know that is controversial to say – I do think we often in English anyway conflate the way we colloquially use the word addicted … like ‘I’m addicted to this show and I’m binge watching it, which is not good for me’.”
He said clinically defined addictions have withdrawal symptoms, while social media does not have that effect, and “those things are different”.

In the landmark US court case centred on the addictive nature of Meta’s products, the company’s lawyer last month conceded to the court that it was “no dispute” people can struggle with social media, but the company has tools to address that. Meta later settled the case for US$18bn while denying any wrongdoing.

articles.title: SMH columnist Peter FitzSimons tells Alan Jones trial alleged victim was ‘revolted’ by abuse
articles.summary: FitzSimons tells court that complainant C told him Jones, who has pleaded not guilty, would touch his penis and he ‘kept pushing it away’

blocks.text: Sydney Morning Herald columnist Peter FitzSimons has told the Alan Jones trial an alleged victim he spoke to in 2019 was “tearful” and sounded “emotionally traumatised” when detailing alleged assaults by the 2GB broadcaster.
The commentator and author gave evidence in the Downing Centre local court on Thursday about a telephone call he had with the alleged victim known as complainant C in October 2019.

He said the man, who remained anonymous to FitzSimons, alleged that Jones, a decade earlier, had pushed him against the wall of a lift and kissed him “romantically” at the broadcaster’s Circular Quay apartment.
C also described a Christmas lunch where Jones was “gripping his penis” under the table, FitzSimons told the court on Thursday.
“He was very tearful … he was very, very upset,” FitzSimons told the Sydney court. “It was clear I was speaking to someone who was emotionally traumatised.”
The journalist said the young man told him that Jones would touch his leg and his penis while he was driving for him.
“He said I didn’t say no … but I kept pushing it away,” FitzSimons said.
Jones has pleaded not guilty to 20 charges of indecent assault and two counts of sexual touching in relation to six men. Eight of the charges relate to complainant C.
FitzSimons said he was put in contact with C by 2GB broadcaster Ray Hadley and he took notes of the conversation on his computer, later sharing them with SMH investigative reporter Kate McClymont.
Hadley has previously told the court the conversation lasted between 30 and 40 minutes.
“He made it clear he was revolted by what happened but he was deeply upset for not being stronger,” FitzSimons said of his phone conversation with C.

FitzSimons said C explained that he was a junior employee at 2GB and in his early 20s and Jones was “the sun king” when he started paying attention to him and complimenting him. Jones eventually offered him a job as a driver.

blocks.caption: Alan Jones (centre) arrives at court on Tuesday. Photograph: Bianca de Marchi/AAP

blocks.text: The court heard C told FitzSimons he was “thrilled to be driving for Jones” and he couldn’t believe the “No 1 person” at 2GB was noticing him.
FitzSimons said C told him that in between the compliments Jones would occasionally give him a “blast”.
After a period of time, Jones began to touch him inappropriately, including at a lunch when he was sitting next to the broadcaster, C said, according to the SMH columnist.
“He said that while he was sitting next to Mr Jones, Mr Jones’s hand went on to his penis and he was gripping his penis,” FitzSimons said on Thursday. “It was under the table.”
The witness said C told him that two men were “laughing at his discomfort” and one of those two senior media identities was 2GB broadcaster Jason Morrison.
FitzSimons said Hadley later told him that C was emotionally fragile and was “spiralling” and he agreed not to pursue a story.
The columnist was later cross-examined by Jones’s barrister Gabrielle Bashir SC.
The court heard that FitzSimons’ contemporaneous notes said C alleged Jones would put his hand on his thigh and then “manipulate my penis”.
Bashir questioned FitzSimons about why he said thigh in one account and knee during his evidence in chief.
“You will appreciate the difference between the knee and the thigh is a matter of two inches,” FitzSimons replied.
The trial before judge Glenn Walsh continues.

articles.title: Iran strikes ships, expands no-go zone outside Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: TEHRAN — Iran said it attacked more than a dozen vessels trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, as it announced an expansion of a no-go zone outside the strategic waterway it…

blocks.text: TEHRAN — Iran said it attacked more than a dozen vessels trying to pass through the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, as it announced an expansion of a no-go zone outside the strategic waterway it has blockaded for months.

The fresh attacks and fighting with the United States sent oil prices above $100 per barrel again as Tehran chokes off the strait and Washington presses a counter-blockade of Iranian ports. Brent oil closed at $101.21.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Wednesday they attacked two US vessels, eight oil tankers, and 10 “non-compliant vessels” that were trying to pass through the route crucial for oil and gas trade, Iranian state media reported.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said “several” vessels in the Gulf of Oman and the Gulf were “subject to disabling fire as part of ongoing military activity in the region”.
The Gulf of Oman lies on the Indian Ocean side of the narrow Hormuz strait, a vital energy conduit that normally carries around a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas.
Iran’s Guards also for the first time added parts of the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea to a new “prohibited zone” on Wednesday, saying exact coordinates will be announced later.
“If a vessel enters that area without coordination, it will be subject to our sanctions,” Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebi told state television.
The Guards also said they struck a US military base in Jordan in response to US forces destroying five Iranian oil tankers a day earlier.
Jordan’s army shot down 18 missiles fired at the kingdom, it said.

Iran’s foreign ministry condemned the attack on its oil tankers as “an overt threat to regional and international peace and security,” saying the strikes “increase the dangers of tensions in the region”.
It said the targeting of US military facilities in the region was “self-defence”.
The US military for its part had said it was responding to an Iranian attack targeting an American warship, the second such incident in less than a week.
Long war?
Iran’s Guards, the ideological arm of the military, said the war could be brought to an end if Washington met its conditions, which included demands on the wars in Lebanon and Yemen.

“It must… refrain from renewed threats, withdraw the Israeli regime’s army from Lebanon, end the blockade of Yemen, release $24 billion in Iran’s frozen assets and refrain from any interference in the country’s nuclear and missile capabilities,” Mohebi said, according to Fars news agency.

Donald Trump, an unpopular president eager to end an unpopular war, asserted Wednesday the conflict will conclude right after the mid-term US elections in November. Polls show his Republican Party could face a drubbing and lose control of one or both houses of Congress.
“I think the war will end immediately after the election” because Iran “can’t hold out any longer,” Trump told journalists, accusing Tehran of being “desperate to try and affect” the vote.
However, the Wall Street Journal quoted US officials saying that Trump’s top advisers are privately warning that the war could drag on through the remaining two years of his term.
Nuclear referral

As Washington tries to choke off Iran economically, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) board of governors on Wednesday voted to refer Iran to the UN Security Council over its nuclear “non-compliance”, in a diplomatic move that piles pressure on Tehran.
The resolution seen by AFP was adopted by a 23-3 vote with eight abstentions, they said. Russia, China and Niger voted against it.
Iran’s representative to the UN nuclear watchdog said the resolution was passed under US pressure, saying it “has no basis and will not bring any results”.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu repeated his claim Iran was about to collapse.
“The main task is to bring down the terror regime in Iran. We are very close to that,” he said Wednesday on a troop visit in southern Syria, where Israel has occupied what it calls a “security zone”.
Tanker strikes

The latest round of US-Iran fighting was triggered after American forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers Tuesday, with the US military saying it “directed the crews to abandon ship” before hitting the vessels.

“Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships, and for every time they do that or try to do that, they’re going to lose tankers, and I think you’ll see that again today,” US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters Tuesday on a visit to Colombia.
Iran has asserted control of the Strait of Hormuz since US-Israeli strikes began the war in February, with traffic through the waterway virtually paralysed.
Tehran requires vessels to obtain permission and pay transit fees before using the strait. /dl

articles.summary: Barry Melrose, a hockey player-turned-coach who led the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final before going on to a long career in broadcasting the sport, has died. He was 70.

image.caption: Barry Melrose speaks to fans in Los Angeles in February 2015. Melrose, a hockey player-turned-coach who led the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final before going on to a long career in broadcasting the sport, has died. He was 70. (Mark J. Terrill/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: NHL·New
Barry Melrose, a hockey player-turned-coach who led the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final before going on to a long career in broadcasting the sport, has died. He was 70.
Melrose stepped away from his analyst role in 2023 after Parkinson's diagnosis
Barry Melrose, a hockey player-turned-coach who led the Los Angeles Kings to the 1993 Stanley Cup final before going on to a long career in broadcasting the sport, has died. He was 70.
ESPN announced Melrose's death Wednesday after his wife informed the network.

"From the flowing locks of his distinctive mullet to the flared lapels of his trademark long suit coats, Barry Melrose cut an unmistakable figure whenever you were fortunate enough to run into him at a rink or catch him on your television screen," NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said. "You were even more fortunate if you engaged him in conversation or listened to his analysis because he never failed to boost your love of the game of hockey."
Melrose stepped away from his analyst role in 2023 after being diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. Wayne Gretzky at the time said Melrose was "bigger than any team."
Melrose had a relatable everyman broadcasting style, bringing a sense of humour to his insights, and was easily recognized by his goatee and slicked-backed hair.

"For decades, Barry Melrose was one of the most distinctive and trusted voices in hockey," ESPN said in a statement. "His knowledge of the game was deep, his candor was refreshing and his passion was unmistakable."

From rural Kelvington, Sask., Melrose broke into professional hockey with the Cincinnati Stingers of the now-defunct World Hockey Association in 1976. He played three seasons in Cincinnati, the last alongside a young Mark Messier, and after the WHA folded, made the transition to the NHL with Winnipeg in 1979.
Melrose went on to play for Toronto and Detroit, where he ended his career after the 1985-86 season.

He finished with 10 goals, 33 points and 728 penalty minutes in 300 career NHL regular-season games, and played seven more games in the playoffs. His WHA totals were five goals, 32 points and 343 penalty minutes in 178 games with Cincinnati.
Melrose turned to coaching and led the Adirondack Red Wings to the American Hockey League's Calder Cup championship in 1992.

The following year, Melrose was hired by the Kings, bringing colorful flare and immediate success to Los Angeles. In his rookie season, he coached a Kings team that featured Gretzky to make a memorable playoff run. They reached the Stanley Cup final before losing to Montreal in five games.
Melrose finished with a record of 79-101 and 29 ties over two-plus seasons in Los Angeles before being fired midway through the 1994-95 season.
Hockey Night in Canada podcast: Barry Melrose on getting fired

He was hired by ESPN in 1996 and later left broadcasting for what became a brief stint coaching the Tampa Bay Lightning in Steven Stamkos' rookie season in 2008-09. Melrose was fired 16 games into the season following a 5-7-4 start and returned to broadcasting.

Melrose was also known for his long-ball hitting prowess in fast-pitch softball, joining fellow Kelvington-area NHL players Wendel Clark, Joey Kocur, Kelly Chase and Kevin Kaminski, among others, during the off-season in Saskatchewan to form what some called the "the toughest team there ever was."

articles.title: Zelensky’s plane ‘almost hit’ by drone en route to Oslo – Norway PM
articles.summary: OSLO — Ukraine and Moldova on Wednesday played down claims from Norway’s prime minister that a plane carrying President Volodymyr Zelensky was almost hit by a drone as it flew to Oslo.…

blocks.text: OSLO — Ukraine and Moldova on Wednesday played down claims from Norway’s prime minister that a plane carrying President Volodymyr Zelensky was almost hit by a drone as it flew to Oslo.
Jonas Gahr Store told Norwegian public broadcaster NRK that Zelensky’s plane was “almost hit by a drone when it was taking off from Moldova”.
But a source in the Ukrainian presidency described the claim that Zelensky was at risk as “exaggerated”.
“It was an alert in Moldova when a Russian (drone) entered Moldovan and Romanian airspace,” the source told AFP.

In Chisinau, government spokesman Dumitru Ciorici said Moldova closed its airspace on Tuesday afternoon just after 4:30 pm local time due to a Russian drone that entered from the direction of Ukraine.
“The airspace was closed to protect aircraft flying over Moldova at the time: three departures and four arrivals were delayed as a result,” he added.
“After 1720, the authorities confirmed that the drone had come down and exploded… some 160 kilometres (100 miles) from Chisinau International Airport.
“Flight restrictions were then lifted. For the same reason, the plane of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky took off… later than scheduled.”

Zelensky arrived in Oslo on Tuesday evening and held talks with Store, Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg and Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide on Norwegian military aid, including air-defence support, and civilian assistance.
On Wednesday, he joined a host of other foreign dignitaries at the funeral of Norway’s King Harald, who died on August 28 aged 89.
Zelensky left Norway afterwards, headed for Canada and talks with leaders there, Store told NRK. /dl

articles.title: Prosec opposes expert verification of open-source evidence in ICC trial
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Prosecutor at the International Criminal Court (ICC) has opposed the request of former President Rodrigo Duterte’s defense team to require expert verification…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Office of the Prosecutor at the International Criminal Court (ICC) has opposed the request of former President Rodrigo Duterte’s defense team to require expert verification in submitting publicly available or open source materials submitted as evidence in trial.

Duterte’s defense team previously proposed an amendment to the international court’s E-Court Protocol to include an expert report to accompany all forms of open source and user-generated evidence to be submitted at the trial, citing the need to avoid “being overwhelmed by material of dubious relevance, authenticity and reliability.”

“It is unreasonable, unnecessary and against the interests of judicial efficiency, to require an expert report to accompany all forms of open source and user-generated evidence,” ad interim Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang asserted in a letter dated September 9.
Niang noted that due to the broad definition of open source information, the need to call for expert verification on a piece of user-generated evidence should instead be made on a case-by-case basis.

These cases that require experts, Niang enumerated, may include disputes on whether the open source evidence is “edited in any way” or if “[artificial intelligence] tools were used to filter the evidence.”
He added that such verification need not apply to publicly available information from reputable sources.

“The Prosecution submits that expert evidence is not necessary to accompany certain other forms of open source evidence from reputable sources. For example, reports from organisations such as the United Nations, government websites, NGOs such as Human Rights Watch, and reputable news publications should not require expert evidence in order to be submitted,” Niang said.
Niang pointed out that the chambers of the ICC have previously allowed open source evidence from reputable sources without an expert report.
Further, Niang asserted that the defence will have the opportunity to challenge the admissibility of open source evidence upon introduction during the trial.
“The Prosecution agrees with the Defence that the Court must be vigilant in its assessment

of open source evidence in the age of artificial intelligence and disinformation… However, the Prosecution submits that the Court must be proportionate in its response to these concerns and not create significant burdens that unnecessarily hamper judicial efficiency and ultimately, risk delaying the start of the trial,” the prosecutor pressed.
As of September 3, the prosecution has intended to disclose over 25,000 pieces of evidence, and it expressed intention to disclose 200 gigabytes of material.

Duterte is awaiting trial on November 30, 2026 at the ICC for two counts of murder as crimes against humanity, and one count of murder and attempted murder as a crime against humanity for his supposed role in the drug war during his presidency and when he was mayor in Davao City. /jpv

articles.title: Skilled migrant women facing barriers in Australia
articles.summary: MELBOURNE — Back home in Uganda, Diana Kyomugisha helped support orphaned children and widows as a social worker.She studied social sciences and social work at university and built up a strong…

blocks.text: MELBOURNE — Back home in Uganda, Diana Kyomugisha helped support orphaned children and widows as a social worker.She studied social sciences and social work at university and built up a strong skill set.
“I was involved in supporting orphans and widows, to connect them with services to advocate for their needs,” Ms Kyomugisha told AAP.
“Sometimes they were mistreated by their relatives, when their husbands would die, they take over their property, or the children are not going to school.”
But when she moved to Australia two-and-a-half years ago, she was forced to work as a cleaner to earn money.
Ms Kyomugisha said she faced several barriers to continuing her skilled career in her new home, the largest being the financial cost of a skills assessment.
“I needed guidance, for a degree, on the standards here, I didn’t know what documentation they needed, I didn’t have any references, I had completely no knowledge,” she said.
She now works as a support worker in aged care and said her journey had caused her to lose confidence in the skills she had built up back in Uganda.

More than 340,000 migrant and refugee women are working below their level of skill and qualification, and they are 20 percent more likely to have their skills underutilized than migrant men, a report released earlier this year found.
The Activate Her Skills report revealed migrant women were earning 31 per cent less than Australian-born women with similar qualifications.

Ms Kyomugisha is one of 160 women engaged in a pilot program to address many of these issues, the Women’s Employment Skills Pathway Program by Settlement Services International (SSI), which is funded by Minderoo.
The Australian-first initiative aims to address gendered barriers in the skills recognition system, by providing personalised support through navigator hubs.

SSI chief executive Violet Roumeliotis said Australia was not taking advantage of highly-skilled migrant women, who were trapped “behind a maze” of exorbitant fees, stretched out timelines and unclear systems.
“The skills qualification system is very flawed, very convoluted, complex, unfair, and expensive, and women are particularly disadvantaged,” she said.
The program is based on a model from Germany, and offers support to migrant women as they navigate the skills and qualification system, to help re-enter their professions.
Ms Roumeliotis said she was speaking to federal and state employment ministers about rolling out the program more widely.
The initiative is building an evidence base about the barriers migrant and refugee women face, and the types of support that can be most effective, Minderoo said.

“Every woman, regardless of her background, should have a fair opportunity to participate in the economy, realize the value of her skills and qualifications, and pursue her career ambitions,” Minderoo chief executive John Hartman said. /dl

articles.title: Jacqui Lambie says Pauline Hanson a ‘bloody coward’ after One Nation cartoon calling Andrew Hastie a traitor
articles.summary: Lambie, a veteran and Tasmanian senator, says One Nation leader is showing her ‘true colours’

blocks.text: Jacqui Lambie has accused Pauline Hanson of being a “coward” for a One Nation cartoon calling the Liberal frontbencher Andrew Hastie a traitor, amid a growing spat between the One Nation leader and the former SAS captain.

Lambie, a veteran and Tasmanian senator, defended Hastie on Thursday, after he called on Hanson to take ownership for a One Nation animated cartoon on social media in which he is repeatedly described as a traitor for giving evidence against Victoria Cross recipient Ben Roberts-Smith in his failed defamation case.
Senior Liberals also joined condemnation of the cartoon on Thursday, with the opposition leader, Angus Taylor, calling for it to be taken down.
Hastie has challenged Hanson and Nationals defector Barnaby Joyce to take responsibility for the One Nation video, promising a costly political battle.
Lambie told ABC radio the cartoon should be immediately taken down and that Hanson was now showing her “true colours”.
“What she’s doing in those cartoons is absolutely disgusting. They are full of bloody violence,” Lambie said.
“But attacking Andrew Hastie, a veteran that has served in our Afghanistan war, or any other veteran, is the lowest ebb you can possibly do. That woman is nothing less than a bloody coward.

“I tell you what, you’re seeing her true colours start to shine now. You watch this, the Australian people. Here comes coward Hanson … And any veteran out there thinking about voting for One Nation or standing for them, I tell you what, you had better think twice.”

Hastie is an SAS veteran and served twice in Afghanistan but has attracted the ire of One Nation and Hanson’s billionaire backer, Gina Rinehart, after he gave evidence against Roberts-Smith in a failed defamation case against Nine newspapers.
Hanson and Rinehart say Roberts-Smith is being unfairly targeted over war crimes allegations related to his service between 2009-2012.
Hastie on Thursday ruled out legal action against Hanson, due to Rinehart’s backing.
“I think it shows [Hanson] to be weak and glass-jawed. I gave her the opportunity to either own her words publicly or to take it down. She chose neither,” he told ABC radio.
“She’s not fit to govern this country. And she’s also cast a massive slur on veterans around the country who think that Australian soldiers should hold high standards of conduct on the battlefield.

“I’m not after legal action, particularly when she’s financed by Australia’s richest person. Why would I walk into a fight that I can’t win financially? But yes, I’m going to impose costs politically.”

Hanson again claimed she had not personally called Hastie a coward, despite posting the video on her social media accounts. Yesterday she told The Nightly newspaper that she would call Hastie a “wanker” instead.
after newsletter promotion
Taylor also called on Hanson to take down the cartoon during a press conference, and said it was wrong for it to remain online.
“Andrew Hastie has served this country with distinction as an officer in the SAS. She should take it down,” Taylor said.
The opposition leader declined to back Hastie’s description of Hanson as “weak and glass-jawed”.
Greens senator David Shoebridge also blasted Hanson, telling News24 it was disgraceful to attack the Liberal frontbencher for giving evidence to a trial under oath.

“I disagree with pretty much everything that comes out of Hastie’s mouth, like his whole suite of policies are things that I tend to oppose … but for the life of me, I can’t work out how any political party can stand by an attack on somebody because they go into court and they tell the truth as they understand it,” he said.
“I mean it’s actually pretty fucking disgraceful to attack him for that.”
James Paterson, the shadow defence minister, said Hanson and her strategist James Ashby “should be ashamed of themselves.”
“I would never dream of accusing someone who has served in uniform for our country of being a traitor,” he said.

“There’s no graver accusation to make, particularly about someone like Andrew Hastie. Andrew Hastie signed up to the ADF after 9/11. He signed up to fight Islamist terrorists as part of the global war on terror. He served on the front lines in Afghanistan over multiple tours. What service has anyone in One Nation given that compares in any way, shape or form to Andrew Hastie’s service?”
